name: The New York Times
justification: The New York Times is a national daily newspaper whose chief theater critics (Ben Brantley 1996 to 2020, Jesse Green as co-chief from 2017 and chief to 2025) are staff critics. Its consensus gap (11.6) and bias (-0.9) define the reference range. Nothing found argues for a change; keep T1 in New York. London coverage is occasional (16 reviews) and lon2 stays.

name: New York Stage Review
justification: New York Stage Review is an independent New York review site whose About page describes its writers as professional drama critics and long-time members of the New York Drama Critics Circle with former newspaper affiliations, with Steven Suskin as publisher and Jesse Oxfeld as editorial director. Frank Scheck, David Finkle and Elysa Gardner are current Drama Critics Circle members and Bernardo, Sommers and Suskin are emeritus members; 11 of its 16 critics also have 3+ reviews at other T1/T2 outlets. Its critics are established but it is a small independent site rather than a major publication, so T2 fits. Keep.

name: Variety
justification: Variety is a national entertainment trade publication whose New York theatre reviews have long been written by staff and contract critics. Marilyn Stasio was a voting New York Drama Critics' Circle member as Variety's critic, and David Rooney and Charles Isherwood have held chief-critic posts at major outlets. Show Score lists 44 percent of its reviews on the 32 complete Show Score shows, in line with the NYT (0.44), and 11 of its 32 critics also write for other T1/T2 outlets. It matches T1 in New York; London volume is small, so London stays T2.

name: Newsday
justification: Newsday is a major Long Island and New York daily newspaper. Its longtime critic Linda Winer reviewed there from 1987 to 2017 and was a voting member of the New York Drama Critics' Circle while at Newsday (now emeritus). Its reviews in our data end in 2019, so it is a historical outlet and keeps the tier that matched its standing as a NYDCC-member daily. Show Score pickup is not usable (only 14 eligible shows).

name: Theater Life
justification: TheaterLife.com is a New York and Hamptons theater site launched in May 2006 by publisher Patrick Christiano, with a named editor in chief, supervising editor, managing editor and contributing writers. Its publisher and editor in chief are voting members of the Drama Desk, and contributor David Sheward is a former Drama Desk president and member of the New York Drama Critics' Circle and Outer Critics Circle. Show Score lists 21% of 33 eligible reviews (weak evidence), and 3 of its 12 critics also review regularly for T1/T2 outlets; the credentialed masthead and 19 years of sustained coverage keep it at T2 under the default-keep rule.

name: Scheckontheater
justification: Scheck on the Arts was a personal blog of Frank Scheck, with 18 reviews in 2011; the domain no longer resolves. It is single-author, which alone would suggest T4, but Scheck is a recognized critic: New York Post theatre critic, Hollywood Reporter reviewer, and former Christian Science Monitor theatre critic. The T4 definition excludes outlets with recognized-critic status, so keep T3 as a defunct outlet.

name: Talkin' Broadway
justification: Talkin' Broadway is a US theatre website live since January 1997, with a named editor (Ann Miner) and reviews written by volunteers. Its main New York critic Matthew Murray began reviewing there in 2000, joined the Drama Desk in 2002 and was an associate editor at TheaterMania. Show Score picks up its reviews at about the same rate as the NYT (0.46 of 41) and its consensus numbers match the reference outlets. Long-serving critics, an editor and nearly 30 years of sustained coverage fit T2 despite the volunteer model; keep.

name: Backstage
justification: Backstage is a long-running US performing-arts trade paper. Its reviewers were staff critics: David Sheward was managing editor, chief theatre critic and later executive editor, served several years as Drama Desk president, and is a member of NYDCC, Outer Critics Circle and ATCA. Backstage stopped publishing reviews in April 2013, so it is defunct as a review source and keeps the tier it held then. Keep T2.

name: The Hollywood Reporter
justification: The Hollywood Reporter is a major US national entertainment trade publication. Its longtime chief theater critic David Rooney (now chief film critic, still reviewing Broadway) is a New York Drama Critics' Circle member and formerly Variety's chief theatre critic. Six of its nine critics also have 3+ reviews at other T1/T2 outlets. Keep T1 NYC; London volume is 4 reviews, so keep T2 there.

name: Did They Like It
justification: Did They Like It is primarily a review aggregator for Broadway and Off-Broadway. In 2021 it added a five-member cohort of original critics led by Jose Solis, including Christian Lewis and Juan Michael Porter II, and the 40 reviews here (2021 to 2022) are from that cohort. Because the id is an aggregator that briefly published its own reviews, keep the current tier rather than re-rate it.

name: New York Daily News
justification: The New York Daily News is a major New York tabloid daily. Joe Dziemianowicz was its staff theatre critic from 2006 to 2018 and is Vice President of the New York Drama Critics' Circle. Its scores sit close to consensus (gap 9.7, bias -2.0); the Show Score sample (19 shows) is too small to use. It fits T2 as an established outlet with a recognized staff critic; its theatre coverage has thinned since 2018, so no case for T1.

name: Time Out New York
justification: Time Out New York is the New York edition of the international Time Out listings and culture brand, with a staff chief theater critic. Adam Feldman, its chief theater critic and theater editor on staff since 2003, has been president of the New York Drama Critics' Circle since 2005. Show Score lists 63% of 30 eligible reviews and its consensus gap (11.0) is in the reference range. Keep nyc1; it has no London reviews in this id (Time Out London is a separate id), so lon3 is kept unchanged.

name: The Wall Street Journal
justification: The Wall Street Journal is a national daily whose drama critic post was held by Terry Teachout from 2003 until his death in 2022 and then by Charles Isherwood, a former New York Times critic. Show Score lists 45 percent of its reviews on 33 complete shows, similar to the NYT reference of 0.44. The consensus gap is high, but a contrarian national critic is still a market-setting voice. Keep T1; no London reviews.

name: The Washington Post
justification: The Washington Post is a major US national newspaper whose chief theater critics (Peter Marks to end of 2023, then Naveen Kumar) reviewed Broadway regularly. Marks left in a buyout on Dec 31, 2023 and the Post eliminated the chief theatre critic role in its Feb 2026 layoffs, so its theatre reviewing has largely stopped. Per the defunct rule it keeps the tier it held while publishing, which was a national staff-critic voice. Keep T1 NYC; no London reviews.

name: The Wrap
justification: TheWrap is a US entertainment-industry news publication; its theatre reviews are almost all by Robert Hofler, its staff Theater Critic. Hofler is a former Variety editor and author, and won an LA Press Club award for theater criticism. Show Score lists 38% of 24 eligible reviews and its scores run harsher than consensus (gap 15.5, bias -8.6), but it is a paid professional critic at an established outlet, which fits T2. Keep.

name: DC Theatre Scene
justification: This id mixes two publications: 85 reviews are from dctheatrescene.com (DC Theatre Scene, almost all by Jonathan Mandell) and 57 from dcmetrotheaterarts.com (DC Metro Theater Arts, now DC Theater Arts, by Richard Seff and Deb Miller). DC Theatre Scene ran from 2005 to December 31, 2020 under editor and publisher Lorraine Treanor, who paid writers until the pandemic cut revenue; DC Theater Arts is an active Washington site that keeps a New York reviewer. All three main critics (Mandell, Seff, Miller) are on the Outer Critics Circle roster. Because the id mixes two outlets, keep T2 and split the id before judging each.

name: Broadway News
justification: Broadway News is a Broadway trade publication published by Broadway Brands, with an executive editor (Ruthie Fierberg, an OCC member) and paid contributors including Brittani Samuel, Naveen Kumar and Gordon Cox. Its critics include Charles Isherwood (former NYT critic, a current NYDCC voting member) and Samuel (George Jean Nathan Award 2023-24). Did They Like It? lists Broadway News among its core outlets next to the NYT and Variety on Maybe Happy Ending (2024) and Just in Time (2025), though not on the 2026 pages checked, matching our data ending April 2025. Market-setting critics and core-aggregator placement support keeping T1; the trade-site format and possible end of reviewing keep confidence at medium.

name: Vulture
justification: Vulture is the culture site of New York magazine, with staff lead critics. Sara Holdren (George Jean Nathan Award winner) and Jackson McHenry are its co-lead theater critics, and Jesse Green held the post before moving to the New York Times. Show Score lists 51 percent of its reviews on shows where Show Score's list is complete, in line with the NYT reference. It sets the market verdict, so keep T1; it has no London reviews.

name: Deadline
justification: Deadline (Deadline Hollywood) is a major US entertainment trade publication. Its Broadway reviews came from Jeremy Gerard (executive editor and chief theater columnist 2014-2016, previously chief drama critic at Variety and Bloomberg and a past president of the New York Drama Critics' Circle) and then Greg Evans, a freelancer who also writes for Variety and Billboard. Show Score data is too thin to use (13 eligible); both of its main critics also have 3+ reviews at other T1/T2 outlets, and its consensus gap (12.0) and bias (+3.1) match the reference range. A national trade with recognized critics fits T1; keep.

name: New York Post
justification: The New York Post is a daily tabloid owned by News Corp with about 117,000 average print copies. Its current critic Johnny Oleksinski is a staff entertainment critic covering film and theater and a voting member of the New York Drama Critics' Circle; Elisabeth Vincentelli also has 32 New York Times reviews in our data. Its consensus gap (13.6) is close to the reference range; Show Score sample is too small to use. Keep nyc2/lon2.

name: TheaterMania
justification: TheaterMania is a long-running US theatre news and review site with a staff chief critic. Zachary Stewart has been its chief critic since 2013 and is vice president of the New York Drama Critics' Circle and a Drama Desk voting member. Show Score lists 62% of its reviews on 61 eligible shows and its consensus gap and bias sit inside the reference range. That is an established professional outlet, so keep T2.

name: NBC New York
justification: NBC New York (nbcnewyork.com) is the website of WNBC, NBC's owned New York TV station, and its theater reviews in our data run 2013 to 2017. The station's own pieces describe Robert Kahn and Dave Quinn as 'NBC 4 New York theater writers', so the reviews came from station writers at a major local broadcaster. I found no critics' body membership or aggregator quoting for Kahn (he is not on the OCC roster), and Show Score data is too thin. Defunct coverage keeps its standing; with a major-outlet byline but unverified critic standing, keep T2 at low confidence.

name: Front Row Center
justification: The Front Row Center is an independent New York review site created and edited by Tulis McCall, whose About page is a personal manifesto and whose Authors page presents contributors mainly as actors, playwrights and producers rather than working critics. None of its top critics (McCall, Walters, Friedman, Campion) is on the Outer Critics Circle roster, and one contributor (Edward Kliszus) lists ATCA membership. Did They Like It? does not list it on the 2024 to 2026 show pages checked, and Show Score lists 32% of eligible reviews. This matches the T3 definition of a multi-contributor specialist site with an editor rather than T2's recognized or paid critics, so move to nyc3.

name: Theater Scene
justification: TheaterScene.net is a New York theatre review site founded and published by Jack Quinn, with Victor Gluck as Editor-in-Chief since 2014. Gluck was a Back Stage drama critic from 1980 to 2006 and is a voting member of the Drama Desk, Outer Critics Circle and ATCA. Show Score lists 63 percent of its eligible reviews (46 shows), similar to established outlets, and 5 of its 28 critics also review regularly at T1/T2 outlets. Its consensus bias is mildly positive (+4.1). I could not verify whether contributors are paid, but the editor, credentialed lead critic and aggregator pickup support keeping T2.

name: Entertainment Weekly
justification: Entertainment Weekly is a US national entertainment magazine owned by People Inc. (formerly Dotdash Meredith, an IAC business), digital-only since its April 2022 issue. It has employed named theater critics, such as Melissa Rose Bernardo, identified as EW's theatre critic in 2006-2007. Its consensus gap (9.8) is within the reference range though its bias (+6.3) is on the kind side, and Show Score eligibility is too small to read (17 shows). It is a major national brand whose theater coverage is a minor part of its remit, which fits T2; keep.

name: amNewYork
justification: amNewYork is a free New York City newspaper owned by Schneps Media, now printed three times a week, with a long-running theater critic, Matt Windman. Windman is a voting member of the New York Drama Critics' Circle and wrote a book of interviews with theater critics. The outlet runs harsher than consensus (-6.1), but a Circle member writing for a city paper fits T2; keep.

name: Chicago Tribune
justification: The Chicago Tribune is a major US metropolitan daily; nearly all its reviews here are by Chris Jones, its chief theater critic since the mid-2000s, who also covers Broadway and was named Broadway critic for the New York Daily News in 2018. Jones is a New York Drama Critics' Circle member, a former Variety touring critic and twice a Pulitzer drama juror. Its consensus gap (9.9) is low. Strong T2; keep.

name: Theatrely
justification: Theatrely is a New York theatre news and review site with a masthead: editor-in-chief Kobi Kassal, senior editor Alan Koolik, chief critic Juan A. Ramirez and senior critic Joey Sims. Sims has written for the NYT, Vulture and TheaterMania and is an OCC member listed under Theatrely, as is Christian Lewis (also Variety, TheaterMania). Did They Like It? lists Theatrely among its core outlets on every Broadway page checked from 2024 through August 2026, next to the NYT, Variety and TheaterMania. An editor, recognized critics and steady aggregator pickup meet T2, so keep with high confidence.

name: USA Today
justification: USA Today is a US national daily owned by USA Today Co. (formerly Gannett). Its long-time theater critic Elysa Gardner is a Drama Desk board member and chaired the 2017 Pulitzer drama jury; Charles Isherwood also reviewed for it. Its Show Score sample is too small to read (11 shows). It does not lead Broadway reception the way T1 outlets do, but its national reach and credentialed critics support T2. Keep.

name: NY1
justification: NY1 is the Spectrum (Charter) 24-hour local news channel in New York City. Its critic Roma Torre is an Emmy-winning journalist and theater critic who left NY1 in 2021; our NY1 reviews run 2010 to 2020. A staff broadcast critic for a major local outlet fits T2; its consensus bias of +5.5 and the lack of found critics' body membership do not support T1. Keep T2 as a historical outlet.

name: The Guardian
justification: The Guardian is a major UK national newspaper with staff theatre critics in London and New York. Its chief theatre critic Arifa Akbar succeeded Michael Billington, and its New York reviews come largely from Alexis Soloski, a New York Times culture critic and George Jean Nathan Award winner. It is a market-setting national publication in both markets. Keep.

name: New York Theater
justification: New York Theater (newyorktheater.me) is Jonathan Mandell's personal theater site, not affiliated with the New York Times; the about page describes it as his blog with no other editor. Mandell is a member of the Drama Desk and the Outer Critics Circle and has written for the New York Times, Washington Post and New York magazine. That makes him a long-serving recognized critic, which fits T2 despite the single-author format; consensus gap 9.6 is inside the reference range. Show Score lists 65% of 37 eligible reviews. Keep nyc2/lon2.

name: The Komisar Scoop
justification: The Komisar Scoop is the personal site of investigative journalist Lucy Komisar, a single-author outlet. Komisar says she is a member of the Drama Desk, and she is an award-winning journalist (Gerald Loeb Award) who has written for The Nation and the Wall Street Journal. A single-author site would normally be T4, but her Drama Desk membership is recognized-critic status; the consensus gap is high (14.7). Keep T3.

name: BroadwayWorld
justification: BroadwayWorld is the largest theatre news site, founded 2003 and published by Wisdom Digital Media, with regional editions across 100 US cities and a West End section. Its reviews come from a large pool of contributors (106 distinct critics in our data) under named chief critics; Michael Dale was its first Chief Theatre Critic for over a decade. Wikipedia treats it as unreliable because it mixes press releases and user content, and Show Score pickup is low (20% of 61) with only 5 of 106 critics established at T1/T2 outlets, but its consensus gap (11.5) and bias (+2.0) sit inside the reference range. Mixed signals do not clearly put it in another tier, so keep.

name: Associated Press
justification: The Associated Press is the largest US wire service, and its theatre reviews are syndicated nationally (sample URLs include ABC News reprints). Mark Kennedy was hired back in 2010 as AP's theatre writer and reviewer; his predecessor Michael Kuchwara held AP's New York Drama Critics' Circle seat. Bias is +6.6, slightly kinder than established critics, but reach and staff-critic status fit the national tier. Keep; Kennedy's own critics'-body membership was not verified.

name: New York Theatre Guide
justification: New York Theatre Guide is a theater news and review site in the TodayTix Group alongside Show-Score and London Theatre, with a named editorial team. Senior editor Gillian Russo is an Outer Critics Circle member, and critic Joe Dziemianowicz was the New York Daily News theatre critic 2006-2018 and is vice president of the New York Drama Critics' Circle. Show Score lists 54% of 46 eligible reviews (same corporate group, weak evidence), and 14 of its 29 critics also review regularly for T1/T2 outlets; the critic credentials alone support T2. Keep.

name: 1 Minute Critic
justification: 1 Minute Critic is a small theater review site owned by Wexler Communications and founded by Matthew Wexler, with several named contributors. Wexler is a member of the American Theatre Critics Association and an alum of the National Critics Institute; 4 of its 10 critics also have 3+ reviews at another T1/T2 outlet. Show Score lists 5% of 21 eligible reviews. A multi-contributor specialist site with a recognized founder fits T3. Keep.

name: Bloomberg
justification: Bloomberg News ran New York theatre reviews in its Muse arts section with staff drama critics: John Simon from June 2005 to November 2010, then Jeremy Gerard handling the major reviews, with editors contributing. Its theatre coverage in our data ends in 2018. The publication is major and international, and its critics were recognized (Gerard is a past New York Drama Critics' Circle president), which is an argument for T1, but Show Score data is too thin to judge (5 eligible) and the consensus gap is high (15.6). The evidence does not clearly require a move, so keep T2 as the defunct-section default.

name: The Daily Beast
justification: The Daily Beast is a national US news and culture site. Nearly all its reviews are by Tim Teeman, a senior editor and the site's theater critic, formerly Arts and Entertainment Editor and US correspondent at The Times of London, with multiple press club awards. I found no critics' body membership for him, and Show Score pickup is not usable (14 eligible). A paid staff critic at a national outlet fits T2; nothing found supports a move. Keep T2.

name: NJ Newsroom
justification: NJ Newsroom was an online New Jersey news site; nearly all its theater reviews (2009 to 2015, now inactive in our data) are by Michael Sommers, who was the Star-Ledger's critic and now reviews for New York Stage Review. An experienced critic writing for a small regional news site fits T3; keep.

name: Pages on Stages
justification: Pages on Stages is a WordPress.com site written entirely by Mason Pilevsky, a sound designer who calls himself a lifelong scholar of theatre; the About page names no editor and no critics'-body membership. That profile resembles T4, and its bias of +6.2 leans kind. However Show Score lists 57% of its reviews on 21 eligible shows, which is real aggregator pickup, and the T4 definition requires none. Keep T3 as a borderline case.

name: Towleroad
justification: Towleroad is an LGBTQ news and culture blog whose theatre reviews in our data were all written by Naveen Kumar between 2015 and 2019. Kumar has since become the Washington Post's theatre critic and has reviewed for the NYT and Variety, so the critic is well established. Theatre is a side beat at the outlet itself, so T2 is not supported and T4 would undervalue the critic; keep T3.

name: Observer
justification: This id mixes two publications: the New York Observer (observer.com, 164 NYC reviews by Rex Reed, David Cote and others) and the UK Sunday paper The Observer (observer.co.uk and theguardian.com URLs, London reviews by Susannah Clapp). Per the rules, keep and flag for a split. The NY Observer side has recognized critics (Cote is a NY Drama Critics' Circle member; Reed was a long-time Observer critic until his death in 2026) and fits nyc2; the UK Observer is a national Sunday paper whose critic Clapp has reviewed since 1997, fitting lon1.

name: Stage Left
justification: Stage Left was a website and weekly newsletter covering New York performing arts, written by founder Rob Russo, who describes himself as a Drama Desk voting member; it closed in 2021 when he became a producer. It was a single-author site, which leans T4, but the author held recognized-critic status while publishing, so the T4 definition does not fully apply. Defunct outlets keep their standing; keep T3.

name: The New York Sun
justification: The New York Sun was bought by Dovid Efune in November 2021 and relaunched as a digital news outlet in February 2022 with Seth Lipsky as editor and a newly hired staff. Nearly all its reviews are by Elysa Gardner, a Drama Desk board member, former USA Today critic and 2017 Pulitzer drama jury chair. Its Show Score sample is too small to read (12 shows) and its bias is +6.6, which argues against moving up, but the critic's standing and the edited newsroom support keeping T2.

name: Front Mezz Junkies
justification: Front Mezz Junkies is a single-author WordPress theatre blog by Ross (Steven Ross), who says he is not a writer by trade and has no editor. However, the Outer Critics Circle critics roster lists 'Ross, Steven' with the affiliation Front Mezz Junkies, and his blog posts describe him as a voting OCC member. T4 is for blogs with no recognized-critic status, so OCC membership takes it out of T4 even though it is a one-person blog. Its scores run kind (+7.0 bias, gap 10.6 within reference), which is a concern but not enough by itself to drop a tier; keep NYC 3 (London has 1 review, keep 3).

name: HuffPost
justification: HuffPost is a major US digital news site, but most of its theater reviews in our data (urls with /_b_ paths) ran on its unpaid contributor blog platform, which HuffPost shut down in January 2018; our data has almost no reviews after that. The writers were established critics: Steven Suskin wrote for Variety and Playbill and founded New York Stage Review, and David Finkle reviews for NYSR. The outlet's standing came from those critics rather than HuffPost editing, which argues against T1 but supports T2 while it published. Keep nyc2/lon2 as a defunct-in-practice outlet.

name: Queerty
justification: Queerty is a US LGBTQ news and entertainment site founded in 2005 and owned by Q.Digital, an employee-owned LGBTQ digital publisher. Theatre coverage is a side strand; most reviews (22 of 29, 2022 to 2024) are by Matthew Wexler, and 83% come from critics established at other outlets. A professional publisher with a contributing theatre critic fits T3; keep.

name: The Stage
justification: The Stage is the UK theatre industry's weekly paper, published since 1880, with an editor and a paid reviews team. In London it is one of the outlets whose verdicts define the market; its New York coverage is a smaller correspondent operation. Mark Shenton and Nicole Serratore (an Outer Critics Circle member listed with The Stage) are established critics. Keep the regional split.

name: Act Three: The Reviews
justification: Act Three: The Reviews is a personal Blogger blog where every visible review is signed by Doug Marino, with no bio, editor or other contributors; it covers Broadway alongside local and high school productions, with an archive back to 2007 and a last visible post in December 2017. The only outside mark is a 'Top 50' theater blogs badge from a ticket site, not a critics' body or aggregator. A search found no other bylines for Marino, and its scores sit far from consensus (gap 20.9, bias -9.5 over 16). A dormant single-author hobby blog fits T4; nyc3 to nyc4 is confirmed (London unused).

name: Cititour
justification: Cititour is a New York City guide site whose theatre reviews come almost entirely from one freelance critic, Brian Scott Lipton. Lipton is listed on the Outer Critics Circle roster as 'Freelance: CitiTour, TheaterMania', is an emeritus member of the New York Drama Critics' Circle, and is a former editor-in-chief of TheaterMania. Second contributor Diane Snyder also writes for The Telegraph in our data. The outlet is small and not listed by Did They Like It?, but its critic is long-serving and recognized, which meets T2, so keep.

name: The Reviews Hub
justification: The Reviews Hub (The Public Reviews from 2007, renamed 2015) is a UK review site with, by its own count, 150 reviewers and 10 editors, including experienced journalists and theatre professionals plus a small number of vetted members of the public. Its executive editor John McRoberts and regional editors are named. Round 1 said its top critics had no recognized standing, but the UK Critics' Circle drama members list includes Scott Matthewman and Maryam Philpott (its film editor), who together wrote 37 of its 160 reviews in our data. With a named editorial structure, sustained coverage since 2007 and Critics' Circle critics among its main reviewers, the case for dropping to T3 is not clear, so keep lon2.

name: All That Dazzles (UK)
justification: All That Dazzles is a UK theatre review site created by Daz Gale in April 2020 during lockdown, now with a team of about 25 reviewers and an editorial quality-control process. It describes its approach as 'positive' with a 'constructive, not cruel' mantra, which matches its kinder-than-consensus scores (bias +5.6). It is a multi-contributor specialist site with an editor, so T3 fits. Keep.

name: As Her World Turns
justification: As Her World Turns is a single-author 'travel photoblog' written by Erica, a soap opera script supervisor; its theatre content in our data is periodic theatre recaps and guides from 2015-2016. Theatre coverage is incidental, there is no editor and no recognized-critic status was found. This matches the T4 definition, so a one-tier move from T3 is proposed.

name: The Village Voice
justification: The Village Voice is a New York alt-weekly founded in 1955 that stopped print in 2017, stopped new content in 2018 and relaunched in 2021 under Street Media. Its chief theater critic Michael Feingold held the post for about three decades to 2013, chaired the Obie Awards (which the Voice runs) and won the George Jean Nathan Award. Defunct-era standing was that of an established professional outlet; keep T2.

name: Theatre's Leiter Side
justification: Theatre's Leiter Side is the personal review blog of Samuel L. Leiter, a theatre historian, Distinguished Professor Emeritus at Brooklyn College and the CUNY Graduate Center, and author or editor of about 31 books. He is a voting member of the Drama Desk and was a Drama Desk Awards nominator 2012-2014; he also reviews for Theater Life and Theater Pizzazz. It is a single-author blog, which alone points lower, but its author has recognized-critic status, so T4 does not fit. Keep T3.

name: Bob's Theater Blog
justification: Bob's Theater Blog is a personal Blogspot blog of capsule reviews and ratings of New York plays, with no named author or bio on the page; it renamed itself Gotham Playgoer on July 8, 2017 and moved to a new address, so this id is defunct. A search for its writer Robert Sholiton found no other bylines, critics' body membership or outside coverage beyond our own site. Its scores track consensus closely (gap 7.8), but closeness to consensus is not standing; a single-author hobby blog without recognition is the T4 definition even while it was active. Move nyc3 to nyc4 confirmed (London unused, left at 3).

name: Wolf Entertainment Guide
justification: Wolf Entertainment Guide was a single-author film and theater site founded in 1998 by William Wolf, who died in 2020. Wolf was the 22nd president of the Drama Desk and chaired the New York Film Critics Circle, so the site carries recognized-critic status that a hobby blog lacks. It runs kind (+6.8) but with an ordinary gap (10.0). Defunct; keep T3 as its standing while active.

name: The Telegraph
justification: The Telegraph is a UK national daily newspaper whose lead theatre critic since 2014, Dominic Cavendish, chaired the Critics' Circle drama section for nine years and then served as Critics' Circle president. It sets the London verdict, so lon1 is kept. Its New York reviews are written by freelancers (Diane Snyder, Matt Wolf) for a UK audience, which fits nyc2. Keep both.

name: Broadway Blog
justification: The Broadway Blog was a multi-contributor New York theatre site covering Broadway, Off-Broadway, the West End and regional theatre with reviews, interviews and news, fronted by Matthew Wexler; its last review in our data is April 2023 and the site no longer responds. Contributor Samuel L. Leiter is a Drama Desk voting member and CUNY Distinguished Professor Emeritus of theatre, but Wexler and other contributors are not on the OCC roster, and I could not confirm an editor title or pay. The evidence fits T3 at least as well as T2 but does not clearly require a move, so keep at low confidence.

name: Los Angeles Times
justification: The Los Angeles Times is a major US national daily; 78 of its 84 rows are by Charles McNulty, its chief theater critic since 2005, who chaired the 2010 Pulitzer drama jury and won the George Jean Nathan Award for Dramatic Criticism. Its consensus gap (10.6) is within the reference range. A staff chief critic at a major national paper fits T1; keep. No London rows, so lon1 is untested and left as is.

name: LouReviews
justification: LouReviews is Louise Penn's London theatre blog, run on a voluntary basis with occasional guest reviewers. A single-author blog would usually be T4, but Penn is a team reviewer for BroadwayWorld UK and Plays International and was invited to join the Critics' Circle in September 2025, which is recognized-critic status. Keep T3.

name: The New Yorker
justification: The New Yorker is a major US national magazine with staff theatre critics. Hilton Als won the 2017 Pulitzer Prize for Criticism for his New Yorker theatre reviews, and Helen Shaw was its theatre critic from 2022 until moving to The New York Times as chief theatre critic in January 2026. Its gap and bias are within the reference range. Keep T1 NYC; no London reviews.

name: Scribicide
justification: Scribicide is a single-author New York theater blog on WordPress.com by Aaron Botwick, inactive since June 2019 in our data; its about page describes it as 'a new york-based theater blog' with a Gmail contact and lists one credential, 'Voting member of the Drama Desk'. That membership would give the author recognized-critic status, but the Drama Desk site blocks fetches and no outside source confirms it, and Botwick is not on the Outer Critics Circle roster. No aggregator pickup was found and its consensus gap (14.4) is above the reference range with neutral bias. On the self-reported Drama Desk status the default keep holds, but if that cannot be confirmed the outlet fits T4.

name: Reviewing The Drama
justification: Reviewing The Drama appears to be a single-author review site; all 20 reviews in our data (2015-2017) are by Robin Riegelhaupt. The site returned 503 and a web search found nothing about the site or its author, so its editorial model, the critic's standing and any outside recognition could not be verified. Scores track consensus (gap 9.9, bias -0.2), and Show Score data is too thin to use (1 eligible). Not enough verified to justify a move; keep.

name: Financial Times
justification: The Financial Times is an international daily newspaper. Its London critic Sarah Hemming is a staff arts writer and theatre critic, formerly theatre editor of The Independent; its New York reviews come from contributors such as Max McGuinness and Brendan Lemon. Consensus gap (9.2) is low. A national paper with a staff London critic fits lon1, and freelance New York coverage fits nyc2; keep.

name: Faster Times
justification: The Faster Times was an online publication whose 5 theater reviews here (2010 to 2011, now defunct in our data) are by Jonathan Mandell, who runs New York Theater and has many reviews at other outlets in our data. Its editorial model could not be verified. Keep T3 as its standing while active.

name: Gotham Playgoer
justification: Gotham Playgoer is Robert Sholiton's personal Blogspot blog, which says it began in 2010 as a way to share impressions with friends; it lists no editor, credentials or other outlets and is still posting in October 2026. Sholiton does not appear on the Outer Critics Circle critics roster, and none of its reviews come from critics with T1/T2 work. A single-author hobby blog without recognized-critic status matches T4, so move NYC 3 to 4. It has no London reviews; London is left as is.

name: Everything Theatre
justification: Everything Theatre is a London review site that calls itself a 100% volunteer-run collective; reviewers get free tickets via official invites and copy is checked by volunteer editorial assistants under head editor Mary Pollard and executive director Rob Warren. None of its named team or top critics appear on the UK Critics' Circle drama members list, and only 1 of its 50 critics has 3+ T1/T2 reviews. An edited multi-contributor site without paid or recognized critics fits T3, not T2. Move London 2 to 3; no NYC reviews.

name: Digital Journal
justification: Digital Journal is a Canadian site that began as a citizen-journalism network with tens of thousands of contributors and a revenue-share model. Its theater reviews are by Markos Papadatos, a contributor focused mainly on country music. Reviews run kind and far from consensus (bias +9.5, gap 18.3 over 27). Incidental theatre coverage from a contributor network fits T4; keep.

name: Staged Theatre
justification: Staged Theatre is a London theatre recommendation and itinerary business that also books tickets and publishes reviews as blog posts. One writer produced 28 of its 30 reviews in our data, and the site names no editor. A commercial single-writer blog with no aggregator pickup fits T4; keep.

name: Theatre Reviews Limited
justification: Theatre Reviews Limited is a small New York review site, originally launched in 1997, run by its two chief critics David Roberts and Joseph Verlezza, who previously ran a professional theatre company. Both are on the 2026-27 Outer Critics Circle roster with this affiliation, and Roberts sits on the OCC executive committee as treasurer. It is a two-critic independent site with no named separate editor, which fits T3. Keep.

name: Culture Sauce
justification: Culture Sauce is Thom Geier's own site, presented on its about page as his commentary on pop culture, mostly theatre. It is effectively single-author, but Geier is a former Entertainment Weekly senior editor and TheWrap executive editor and won a 2024 National Arts and Entertainment Journalism Award for theatre criticism. Show Score lists 58 percent of its reviews on 36 complete shows, above the NYT reference of 0.44. Recognition lifts it above a hobby blog, so keep T3.

name: London Box Office
justification: London Box Office is a theatre ticket retailer whose news section publishes reviews led by head reviewer Stuart King, who says he is a Critics' Circle member and attends press nights. Its scores are near consensus (bias +0.9). Show Score lists none of its reviews on 52 complete shows, which is weak evidence for London. It sells tickets for shows it reviews, which is a conflict worth noting, but the critic standing and sustained coverage fit T2, so keep.

name: Melinda's Malarky
justification: Melinda's Malarky is a personal Blogger site ('Comments & critiques on cultural events and New York City happenings') whose posts range across jazz concerts, tennis fashion and theatre. It is a single-author hobby blog with incidental theatre coverage, no editor and no recognized-critic status found, and its scores sit far from established critics (gap 20, bias -11.7). This matches T4, so a move from T3 is proposed.

name: Exeunt Magazine
justification: Exeunt NYC is the New York arm of Exeunt Magazine (founded in the UK in 2011, NYC site launched 2018), and its own About page calls it 'a writer-driven, all-volunteer website' with editors who take pitches. Despite the unpaid model, its critics have recognized standing: Lane Williamson and Caroline Cao are on the Outer Critics Circle roster under Exeunt, and Nicole Serratore (OCC, The Stage) is a top contributor. Did They Like It? quoted Exeunt (Williamson) on Paranormal Activity in August 2026, and Show Score lists it at the NYT reference rate. Recognized critics and aggregator pickup outweigh the volunteer model for T2, so keep.

name: Theatre Weekly
justification: Theatre Weekly is a London theatre news, review and ticket site whose only named staff member is managing editor Greg Stewart, who wrote 68 of its 98 reviews in our data. It recruits other reviewers through an open Guest Reviewer Programme requiring a love of theatre, two writing samples and two shows a month, with no pay mentioned. Stewart is not on the UK Critics' Circle drama members list and none of its 14 critics have 3+ T1/T2 reviews; its bias is +6.2. That is a semi-pro edited site, T3 rather than T2.

name: West End Best Friend
justification: West End Best Friend is a UK theatre news and review site created during the COVID-19 lockdown by performer James Edge 'to try and spread some positivity', now with an editor-in-chief (Jenny Ell) and about 45 listed contributors, and paid social-media sponsorship packages. No recognized critics found, and its scores run well above established critics (bias +7.6), consistent with its positive mission. It sits at the low end of T3 as a multi-contributor site with an editor; the evidence is not strong enough to drop it to T4. Keep.

name: Off Script with Dan Dwyer
justification: Off Script is Dan Dwyer's site and radio program; he is an independent reviewer of New York and New England theatre whose show airs on NPR affiliate WHDD Robin Hood Radio, whose reviews often appear on The Berkshire Edge, and who is the American reviewer for the German magazine Blickpunkt Musical. It is single-author, but he has outside publication. Keep T3.

name: The Times (UK)
justification: The Times is a UK national daily with a staff chief theatre critic, Clive Davis, and a deputy theatre critic and theatre commissioning editor, Dominic Maxwell. It is one of the London papers whose reviews set the West End verdict, which fits T1 for London; its 24 NYC reviews are occasional and T2 there is reasonable. Keep both.

name: Theatre Bee
justification: Theatre Bee is a single-author London theatre blog where every post is credited to the 'Theatre Bee' persona, and its footer points readers to the author's Show Score profile, which suggests an audience reviewer rather than a credentialed critic. No editor or recognized-critic status was found, and it has 5 reviews from 2022. That matches T4, so move from T3.

name: London Theatre
justification: LondonTheatre.co.uk is a ticketing and editorial site owned by TodayTix Group (via Encore Tickets). Its reviewers are established critics: Matt Wolf was Variety's and the International New York Times' London critic, and Marianka Swain writes for the Telegraph and the i; 13 of its 20 critics also review regularly at T1/T2 outlets. Show Score pickup is 0.73 of 45. The site sells tickets for the shows it reviews and its consensus bias is +7.2, which argues against moving up. Keep T2.

name: Theatre and Tonic
justification: Theatre and Tonic is a UK theatre website founded in 2014 with a Founder and Lead Editor (Emmie Newitt) and co-editors, and says its team reviewed over 800 shows in 2025. Its writers are unpaid: the recruitment page says the roles 'are all voluntary' and asks for reviewers who are 'enthusiastic, positive and dependable', which matches its +10.0 bias against established critics. None of its named writers appears on the UK Critics' Circle drama members list, and no pickup by WestEndTheatre.com, theatre.reviews or londontheatre.co.uk was found. It has an editorial structure, which is the T3 marker, but the volunteer, positivity-seeking model and strong bias point toward T4; the evidence leans down without being clear enough to move, so keep T3 at low confidence.

name: Bsonarts
justification: Bsonarts was a blog by Bruce Smith with 11 reviews in 2017-2018. The domain no longer resolves, and searches found no information about the site or its author. Not enough to judge, so keep T3.

name: The Philadelphia Inquirer
justification: The Philadelphia Inquirer is a major metropolitan daily whose theatre coverage has come from long-serving staff and freelance critics. Howard Shapiro spent decades at the paper including ten years as its Broadway critic, and Toby Zinman has been its freelance critic since 2006, named by American Theatre among the nation's most influential critics. That fits T2; keep.

name: The Spy in the Stalls
justification: The Spy in the Stalls is a London star-rated review site that names no editor, invites readers to join as reviewers and is funded by Buy Me a Coffee donations. Our data has no named critics for it, and its scores run far above established critics (bias +11.7, gap 14.3 over 22 shows). That fits T4. KEEP.

name: BackStage Barbie
justification: BackStage Barbie is an anonymous Blogspot blog whose tagline lists its subjects as theatre, dance, figure skating and sass. It has a single pseudonymous author with no bio, no editor and no credentials, and it ran only from 2015 to 2017 in our data. That is a hobby blog and fits T4 by definition. Move 3 to 4.

name: StageZine
justification: StageZine is a small US theater site combining Broadway reviews and listings with restaurant and travel features (TravelZine), and its homepage fills space with a New York Times theater feed; it names no publisher, editor or masthead, and its footer credits only a marketing firm. Two writers, David NouNou and Scott Harrah, account for all its reviews in our data, and neither appears on the Outer Critics Circle roster or in any other source I could find. With no editorial structure and no recognized critics, T4 fits; keep.

name: A Youngish Perspective
justification: A Young(ish) Perspective is a UK arts review site started in 2022 by Tabitha James, formerly head editor of the Young Perspective, and its about page says 'Our reviewers are volunteers - all with day jobs'. No pay is mentioned and none of its top critics appear on the UK Critics' Circle drama members list; only 1 of 9 critics has 3+ T1/T2 reviews. Its scores run well above established critics (bias +8.9, gap 14.7 over 34 shows), the pattern of fan writing. A small volunteer site with no recognized critics fits T4; move London 3 to 4 (no NYC reviews, NYC unchanged).

name: WhatsOnStage
justification: WhatsOnStage is a London theatre news and review site founded in 1996, which runs the public-voted WhatsOnStage Awards. It has an editor-in-chief (Alex Wood) and a chief critic, Sarah Crompton. It is an established professional outlet, listed by Show Score for 77% of eligible reviews, but it is a specialist site rather than a national paper. Keep T2.

name: North West End
justification: North West End UK is a UK-wide theatre news and review site formed in 2015 to promote amateur and professional theatre equally; its team is described as actors, directors, producers and theatre fans. It has many contributors (14 in our 21 rows) but no named editor or paid critics were found. A multi-contributor enthusiast site sits between T3 and T4; evidence does not clearly support a move, so keep lon3.

name: Liam O'Dell
justification: liamodell.com is the personal website of Liam O'Dell, a deaf freelance journalist who calls himself a theatre critic; his about page says he is a freelance news reporter for indy100 (part of The Independent), that his work has featured in The Guardian, The Stage, The Verge and The Independent, and that he won IPSE's Young Freelancer Award in 2021. It is single-author with no editor, he is not on the UK Critics' Circle drama members list, and no pickup of his reviews by London aggregators was found. Those facts sit close to the T4 definition, but he is a working professional journalist, which keeps him above a hobby blog, and his scores lean harsh (bias -11.3) rather than promotional. The evidence does not clearly support a move, so keep T3 at low confidence.

name: CurtainUp (defunct)
justification: CurtainUp was a US online theatre review magazine edited and published by Elyse Sommer, described by library catalogs as a guide to current theater in New York, Washington and to a lesser extent London; our data runs 1996 to 2020 and the site is now down. It ran a stable of named contributors with Sommer as editor. Contributors in our data include Simon Saltzman, president emeritus of the Outer Critics Circle, and Charles Wright, board president of the Drama Desk. Defunct outlets keep the tier of their standing, and two decades under an editor with recognized contributors fit T2, so keep.

name: Stage and Cinema
justification: Stage and Cinema is a multi-region theatre review site run by Tony Frankel, described by OC Weekly as one of the most widely read theatre sites in Southern California. The same piece says contributors are not paid. It has an editor and many contributors (30 distinct critics in our data), which fits T3, and nothing points to T2 standing, so keep.

name: Daily Mail
justification: The Daily Mail is a UK national daily newspaper. Its theatre critic Patrick Marmion (and earlier Robert Gore-Langton and Georgina Brown) review West End openings as staff or contracted critics. Show Score pickup is 0% of 33, but Show Score covers London thinly, so that is weak evidence; consensus gap (11.8) and bias (-1.0) match the reference range. A national daily with a named staff critic fits T1 in London; keep.

name: Theater Pizzazz
justification: TheaterPizzazz is a NYC theatre and cabaret site founded by Sandi Durell, a Drama Desk and Outer Critics Circle voter and ATCA member, and now run by publisher and editor Eyal Solomon. Its staff page lists about a dozen contributors, several of them Drama Desk voting members (Ron Fassler, Samuel L. Leiter, Alix Cohen, Carole Di Tosti) and Carol Rocamora (OCC, Drama Desk, ATCA). An edited multi-contributor specialist site with recognized critics does not fit the T4 hobby-blog definition; T2 is not supported because pay status is not stated and bias runs +5.5. Move NYC 4 to 3; no London reviews.

name: La Voce di New York
justification: La Voce di New York is an Italian and English online daily founded in 2013, with a named editor-in-chief and a reporting staff. Its theatre reviews come from contributors JK Clarke and Elise Nussbaum, who are not on the staff page. A professional publication whose theatre coverage is a contributor side beat fits T3; keep.

name: readaboutstuff
justification: Read About Stuff is a London theatre review and interview site whose masthead reads 'Dan English - Freelance Theatre Critic'; all reviews and interviews on its homepage are his. There is no editor or other contributor, Dan English is not on the UK Critics' Circle drama members list, and a web search found no bylines for him at other outlets. Its scores run much kinder than consensus (bias +11.2 over 33 shows). A single-author blog with no recognized-critic status fits T4; move London 3 to 4.

name: The Recs
justification: The Recs is a UK-based arts review and recommendations site covering London, UK touring and New York theatre. Its About page says it began as a very casual affair during the Covid pandemic; it names an editor (Steve Coats-Dennis) and a small review team of writers, and says PR firms added it to press lists after a publicist called it a new critical voice. No critic has recognized-body status or T1/T2 crossover (0 of 6), and its scores run kind (bias +8.4); Show Score data is too thin to use (13 eligible). It sits at the low edge of T3 as a small multi-contributor site with an editor; keep.

name: Theater News Online
justification: Theater News Online was a New York review site active 2014 to 2020 in our data; theaternewsonline.com now serves only a parked-domain redirect, the Wayback Machine could not be reached, and searches found no coverage of the outlet, so its owner and editorial model remain unverified. Its writers were established critics: Jeremy Gerard (former Variety and Bloomberg critic, later Deadline), Joe Dziemianowicz (NY Daily News critic) and David Cote (Time Out New York), and Brian Scott Lipton is an Outer Critics Circle member. The roster argues for T2, but the tier is about the outlet, and nothing about the outlet itself could be confirmed, so keep T3.

name: NorthJersey.com
justification: NorthJersey.com is the website of The Record (Bergen County, NJ), a regional daily. Nearly all reviews here are by Robert Feldberg, who Playbill lists as a New York Drama Critics' Circle member for the Bergen Record. A recognized long-serving paid critic at an established paper fits T2. Keep; his current NYDCC status and the paper's ownership were not verified.

name: DC Theater Arts
justification: DC Theater Arts is a nonprofit DC-region performing arts site with a leadership team (Editor in Chief Nicole Hertvik, Executive Editor John Stoltenberg, News Editor, founder Joel Markowitz) and about 70 listed writers. Its New York reviews came from Deb Miller, hired in 2016 as sole NYC correspondent and NY Editor and described by the outlet as a member of the Outer Critics Circle. The site dropped New York coverage in June 2026, but defunct coverage keeps the tier that matched its standing, and an edited multi-writer outlet whose NYC critic is an OCC member fits T3, not T4. The nyc4 to nyc3 move is confirmed.

name: Evening Standard
justification: The Evening Standard (now The London Standard, a free weekly since September 2024, circulation about 150,000) is London's own paper with a staff chief theatre critic, Nick Curtis, who has written on theatre since 1989. Its reviews are central to West End reception and Show Score lists 86% of 37 eligible reviews. T1 for London fits; it has essentially no NYC coverage. Keep.

name: Show Showdown
justification: Show Showdown is a group theatre blog running since 2007 with about a dozen listed contributors, including Wendy Caster and Cameron Kelsall, who also review for other outlets. It has no stated editor or about page. A multi-contributor specialist blog sits between T3 and T4; with established contributors, keep T3.

name: Plays International
justification: Plays International is a UK theatre magazine founded in 1984/85 by former Plays and Players editor Peter Roberts, taken over in 2016 by the Theater Research Institute of Europe and online-only since January 2022, edited by Jeremy Malies. It runs reviews by a team of contributors across London, the UK and abroad. A long-running niche magazine with a named editor fits T3; keep.

name: Stage Buddy
justification: StageBuddy is a New York performing-arts listings and review site whose about page says it has 'the largest database of small-show reviews' and staff 'constantly going out to review', and invites readers to join its review staff; it names no editor or owner. Its top critic Elyse Trevers is on the 2026-27 Outer Critics Circle roster under StageBuddy, and Jose Solis was described by American Theatre as a 'StageBuddy theatre critic' and has written for The New York Times and The Washington Post. Recognized critics on staff keep it above T4, while open recruitment and no named editor keep it below T2; keep T3.

name: London Unattached
justification: London Unattached is a London lifestyle magazine founded and edited by Fiona Maclean, covering theatre alongside restaurants, bars, hotels and travel. Theatre is one strand of general lifestyle content and no critics'-body membership was found for its writers. Its scores run far kinder than established critics (bias +14.2, gap 16.1 over 34 reviews), consistent with promotional writing. Keep T4.

name: Parade
justification: Parade was a nationwide Sunday newspaper magazine (distributed in 700+ US newspapers until 2022, now web-only, owned by The Arena Group). Its 5 theatre pieces in our data are 2018 posts by Janice Kaplan; theatre is an incidental beat and no sustained critic or theatre editor was found. T2 requires sustained theatre coverage by recognized critics, which this does not show, so a move to T3 is proposed. Kaplan's credentials could not be verified (site blocked fetches).

name: Broadway & Me
justification: Broadway & Me is the single-author blog of Janice C. (Jan) Simpson. The Outer Critics Circle critics roster lists 'Simpson, Janice C.' with the affiliation Broadway & Me/Broadway Radio, and CUNY lists her as Arts and Culture Reporting Director at its journalism school and co-host of Theater Talk. T4 is for blogs without recognized-critic status, so her OCC membership puts this one-person blog in T3. Her scores run harsher than consensus (-7.3), the opposite of promotional writing. No London reviews, so London stays 4.

name: This Week in New York
justification: This Week in New York (twi-ny) is a NYC arts and events listings guide that Mark Rifkin started in 2001 as an email to friends; it now runs as a website and Substack. All 57 reviews in our data are by Rifkin, and theatre is one strand of a general city guide. No critics'-body membership was found for him. A single-author general guide fits T4; keep.

name: Lighting & Sound America
justification: Lighting & Sound America is a US trade magazine for the entertainment technology industry; its theatre reviews are written by its editor-in-chief David Barbour, who co-founded it in 2004. Barbour has led the Drama Desk (named co-president in 2024) and spent 14 years editing Theatre Crafts/Entertainment Design. The outlet is a niche trade magazine, but the critic is a long-serving recognized critic, and consensus gap (11.3) and bias (-3.2) are within reference. Keep.

name: The Upcoming
justification: The Upcoming is a London digital magazine launched in 2011 that calls itself a small team, with a public 'Join the team' page and reviews by many different writers without bios (15 critics across 36 reviews). Its scores run far kinder than established critics (bias +16.2, gap 16.7 on 36 shows). No editor or recognized critics were found, so keep T4.

name: Stu on Broadway
justification: Stu on Broadway is Stuart Brown's personal blog of musical theatre commentary and reviews. Single-author blogs default lower, but Brown is president of the Connecticut Critics Circle and a member of the Outer Critics Circle and the American Theatre Critics Association. Recognized-critic status keeps it at T3.

name: The Independent
justification: The Independent is a UK national newspaper, a print daily from 1986 to 2016 and online-only since then. It runs theatre reviews by named critics (Alice Saville is its most frequent reviewer in our data; she also edits Exeunt and freelances for Time Out, The Stage and the FT). Its consensus gap (10.8) is in the reference range. I could not fetch the Independent site to confirm Saville's title. KEEP lon1/nyc2 as a national paper with sustained London coverage.

name: Simon Seez
justification: Simon Seez is Simon Saltzman's personal Blogspot blog (7 reviews, 2016 to 2017). Single-author blogs default lower, but Saltzman was president of the Outer Critics Circle from 2006 to 2018 and wrote for U.S. 1 in Princeton. Recognized-critic status keeps T3.

name: Musical Theatre Review
justification: Musical Theatre Review is a UK website and free quarterly digital magazine launched in spring 2013 by Lisa Martland, a former deputy editor of The Stage, who edited it with a freelance team of four. It is a niche specialist magazine with an editor, and its reviews in our data stop in 2021. Show Score data is too thin to use (13 eligible) and its scores run kind (bias +8.4). That matches T3; keep.

name: Carey Purcell
justification: This id is the personal byline of Carey Purcell, with no domain recorded in our data. Purcell is on the 2026-27 Outer Critics Circle roster as a freelancer for TheaterMania and the Huffington Post, so the writer has recognized-critic standing even though the platform is unclear. Without the URLs the outlet cannot be identified; keep T3.

name: Zeal NYC
justification: Zeal NYC was a New York arts review site whose reviews in our data run 2014 to 2018; the current zealnyc.com appears repurposed and the Wayback Machine could not be reached, so its masthead and editorial model remain unverified. Its second-largest contributor, Chris Caggiano, is an Outer Critics Circle member (listed with The Arts Fuse), but its top contributor Jil Picariello has no verified credentials. One sample URL points to chriscaggiano.com, Caggiano's personal blog, so some rows under this id may be misattributed. With too little verified about the outlet itself, keep T3.

name: Center On The Aisle
justification: Center On The Aisle was a small New York theatre review site with four contributors in our data (2015-2018), led by Meredith Ganzman. The site returned 503 and its about page, editor and critics' credentials could not be verified. Scores track consensus moderately (gap 9.4, bias +5.1) and there are no Show Score eligible reviews. Not enough verified to justify a move; keep.

name: City Cabaret
justification: City Cabaret's own site returned no descriptive content, so its publisher and editorial model could not be verified. All reviews in our data are by Elizabeth Ahlfors, a cabaret journalist who has written for Cabaret Scenes and CurtainUp and sat on the Bistro Awards committee. The site appears to be a single-author outlet, but the critic has some recognized standing in the cabaret field and the scores track consensus closely (gap 6.0). Not enough is verified to justify a move; keep.

name: Reflections in the Light
justification: Reflections in the Light is Lauren Yarger's blog on theater 'with an added Christian perspective', posting sparsely since 2024. Yarger is a member of the Drama Desk (former vice president), the Outer Critics Circle and the American Theatre Critics Association, and was CurtainUp's Connecticut theater editor and a BroadwayWorld contributing editor. Single-author, but with recognized-critic status, so T3 rather than T4; keep.

name: NJ.com
justification: NJ.com is Advance Publications' New Jersey news site; NJ Advance Media supplies content to both NJ.com and The Star-Ledger, and comScore put its audience at about 12.1 million monthly unique visitors in 2017-18. Its main theatre reviewer, Christopher Kelly (56 of 82 reviews), is listed on Muck Rack as Vice President, Content at NJ.com and a former staffer at the Fort Worth Star-Telegram and Texas Monthly, so the reviews come from a senior newsroom journalist, not a volunteer. No critics' body membership was found for Kelly or Ronni Reich, and aggregator pickup cannot be measured (Show Score eligible 1). A large professional newsroom with sustained Broadway coverage and an edited staff fits T2; keep.

name: Chelsea Community News
justification: Chelsea Community News describes itself as an 'independent, single-owner online newspaper' for one Manhattan neighborhood, founded and edited by Scott Stiffler and funded by advertising, grants and reader pledges. Most of its theater reviews are by Michael Musto, a long-time Village Voice columnist in our data, but theater coverage is incidental to a very small community site. T4 fits; keep.

name: NewNowNext
justification: NewNowNext was a pop culture news blog owned by Logo TV (now Paramount), merged into Logo News in July 2022. All 10 reviews are by Michael Musto, who wrote the Village Voice's La Dolce Musto column for almost three decades and a weekly Musto Unfiltered column for NewNowNext. A corporate-owned site with theatre as a side strand, written by a long-established columnist, fits T3; keep as a defunct outlet.

name: Time Out London
justification: Time Out London is the London edition of the Time Out listings and culture magazine. Andrzej Lukowski has been its theatre editor since 2013 and leads a team of freelance critics, several of whom (Tim Bano, Tom Wicker) also review for the Financial Times and The Stage. Show Score lists 71% of 49 eligible reviews. It is a major London verdict-setting outlet; keep T1 for London.

name: Monstagigz
justification: Monstagigz is a one-writer London blog covering music, theatre and cinema; its about page says the writer worked for local newspapers and business media and that the site aims to help readers get in-demand tickets cheapest. No editor or team is named, the writer is not on the UK Critics' Circle drama members list, and none of its critics review elsewhere in our data. A single-author general gig blog with no recognized-critic status fits T4; move London 3 to 4.

name: London Pub Theatres
justification: London Pub Theatres is a niche magazine with an ISSN (2977-6724), published by London Pub Theatres Magazine Ltd and edited by Heather Jeffery, with a team of reviewers covering London's pub theatre scene. It received a special award in February 2024 for providing a forum for pub theatre work. A niche magazine with an editor fits T3; keep. Consensus data is below the 15-review threshold.

name: Out Magazine
justification: Out is a US monthly LGBTQ magazine founded in 1992, owned by Equal Pride, with circulation of about 203,000. Its theater pieces in our data (2015-2019) are mostly by Michael Musto, a longtime Village Voice columnist who appeared as Out's representative on CUNY TV's Theater Talk critics panels. A national niche magazine with occasional theater coverage by a known writer fits T3. KEEP.

name: The Epoch Times
justification: The Epoch Times is an international multi-language newspaper and media company based in New York and affiliated with Falun Gong; its theatre reviews in our data (2015-2017) are mostly by Judd Hollander. Hollander is on the 2026-27 Outer Critics Circle roster listed with the Epoch Times. Theatre is a minor beat at a politically positioned general paper, with one recognized critic, which fits T3. Keep.

name: The Jewish Chronicle
justification: The Jewish Chronicle is a long-established UK national weekly for the Jewish community with a named theatre critic. All 24 reviews are by John Nathan, described as theatre critic for the JC and The Independent and called a distinguished critic in Jewish News. Its scores sit close to consensus (gap 7.0, bias +1.3). It is a community-focused paper and Nathan's Critics' Circle membership could not be verified, so the evidence does not clearly support T2; keep T3.

name: LondonTheatre1
justification: LondonTheatre1 is an independently owned London theatre services business (owner Neil Cheesman) that sells tickets through Encore and ATG affiliate links and publishes news and reviews by its own reviewers. Its two most prolific critics, Chris Omaweng (55 of 125 reviews, reviewing there since 2014) and John Groves (15 reviews), both appear on the UK Critics' Circle drama members list, so most of its reviews come from recognized, long-serving critics. Round 1 said other contributors had no verified standing; Groves contradicts that. Its scores run kinder than consensus (+5.8, gap 14.0), which is a concern but under the +6 flag, so keep lon2.

name: British Theatre Guide
justification: This id mixes two publications: 48 reviews are from britishtheatreguide.info (British Theatre Guide), 9 from britishtheatre.com, and 41 have no URL. British Theatre Guide is a UK-wide review site with a team of regional editors (national editor David Chadderton, London editor Philip Fisher) and about 70 named reviewers, including the top critics in this row (Keith McKenna, Vera Liber, Howard Loxton); Fisher is a Critics' Circle drama section member. britishtheatre.com is a UK theatre news and ticketing site, covering theatre since 1999 and acquired in 2026 by tickadoo. Because the id mixes two outlets, keep and split the id before judging.

name: On Off Broadway
justification: On Off Broadway was a small review site whose 15 reviews in our data (2010) are all by Matt Windman; the domain now redirects to a domain-sale page, so the outlet is defunct. Windman is an established New York critic (amNewYork, also Newsday and New York Stage Review) and author of a book of interviews with theatre critics. A single-author site would point lower, but its critic has recognized standing, so T4 does not clearly fit. Defunct outlets keep their tier; keep.

name: Times Square Chronicles
justification: Times Square Chronicles (T2C) is a New York entertainment website owned and published by Suzanna Bowling, who writes 57 of its 62 reviews in our data. Bowling is on the 2026-27 Outer Critics Circle roster under Times Square Chronicles, and her staff bio says she is a member of the Drama Desk and the Outer Critics Circle and was a nominator; the site also names a cabaret/music/co-theatre editor. That recognized-critic status rules out the T4 definition, and her scores show no promotional lean (bias -1.6, gap 13.0). Against a higher tier, the disclosure page says 'Most of the articles listed as writer, are paid advertorials that help pay to run this site', and no aggregator pickup was found, so move one tier to T3; London has no reviews, so both markets get T3 rather than the round-1 split.

name: The Arts Desk
justification: The Arts Desk is a UK arts site founded in 2009 by professional critics, mainly from national broadsheets, and grew to more than 70 writers. It won the specialist category at the 2012 Online Media Awards. Show Score lists 79 percent of its reviews on 33 complete shows. An established professional outlet with recognized critics fits T2, so keep.

name: Theatrecat
justification: theatreCat is the personal review site of Libby Purves, who started it after serving as chief theatre critic of The Times from 2010 to late 2013. It is a single-author site with no separate editor, which would normally be T4, but its author is a former national chief critic writing to newspaper standards. T3 fits that combination. Keep.

name: Journal Inquirer
justification: The Journal Inquirer is a daily newspaper in Manchester, Connecticut, serving 17 towns, owned by Hearst since 2023. Its 2018 reviews in our data are by Tim Leininger. A local daily paper fits T3. Keep.

name: Labor Press
justification: LaborPress is a New York labor news outlet founded in 2009 by Neal Tepel, whose stated focus is workers' rights, collective bargaining and union news. Its theater reviews (2016-2018) were written by Dr. Leonard Golubchick, listed as its entertainment editor, with no theater critics' body membership found. Theater coverage is incidental to a labor-news publication, which is the T4 definition. Move nyc3 to nyc4.

name: The i
justification: The i is a British national quality daily, founded in 2010 as a sister paper to The Independent and owned by DMG Media since 2019, with a print circulation of about 116,000 (Sept 2025). Its theatre reviews in our data come mostly from Fiona Mountford, who also has reviews in our data at the Telegraph and the Evening Standard. As a national newspaper with a professional critic it fits the London T1 definition. Keep.

name: Fordham Observer
justification: The Fordham Observer is the student newspaper of Fordham University's Lincoln Center campus, with a student editorial board. Its 8 Broadway reviews (2017 to 2018) were written by student writers, with no professional critic status or aggregator pickup. A student paper is a very small non-professional outlet and fits T4; move 3 to 4.

name: Drama Queen NYC
justification: Drama Queen NYC appears to be a single-author theater blog by Jonathan Warman (all 16 rows, 2015 to 2019), running kinder than consensus (bias +8.0). The site returned a server error (522) and no outside information could be gathered, so the T4 case cannot be confirmed. Per the rules, keep and note it as a T4 candidate.

name: Broadway Showbiz
justification: Broadway Showbiz is an active entertainment news website covering theater, film, dance, nightlife and travel; its homepage does not name an owner or editor. Seven of our eight reviews (2015-2017) are by Corine Cohen, and they run much kinder than consensus (bias +13.1, n=8, too few to rely on). Its operator and editorial model could not be verified, so keep.

name: The Contending
justification: The Contending is a film, television and awards site (Oscar predictions are a main section) with three co-founders and a senior writer since its launch on 8/26/2024; theater is one section and Frank J. Avella is its only theater reviewer. Avella's listed memberships are film and LGBTQ critics' groups (GALECA, New York Film Critics Online) and the Dramatists Guild as a playwright; a search found no Drama Desk or Outer Critics Circle membership. The outlet has staff, which argues against T4, but its theater coverage is incidental to a film awards site, it has no aggregator pickup, and its scores run well above established critics (bias +10.2 over 20 shows). Move nyc3 to nyc4 confirmed.

name: First Night Magazine
justification: First Night Magazine is a bilingual (English and Spanish) London theatre site launched in late 2025 whose only named person is Guillermo Nazara, listed under the About menu and credited with its interviews; it has a Support Us page and no named editor, team or contributors. Searches for Nazara with and without the accent found no theatre bylines elsewhere or critics' body membership. Its reviews carry no bylines in our data and sit far from consensus (gap 19.2, bias -14.0 over 23 shows). A single-person site with no recognition fits T4; move London 3 to 4 (NYC unused).

name: Onandoffbroadwaytheaterreviews
justification: This is Richard Seff's single-author review site. Seff is a member of the Outer Critics Circle and has written for DC Theater Arts, which is recognized-critic status. Keep T3.

name: 2ontheaisle
justification: Two on the Aisle is Karen Isaacs's personal WordPress blog of New York and Connecticut reviews. Isaacs is a founding member and secretary of the Connecticut Critics Circle, a member of the Outer Critics Circle, and writes a theater column for Shore Publications. A single-author blog by a recognized critic sits at T3. KEEP.

name: New York Classical Review
justification: New York Classical Review is a classical music review site launched in 2013 by Lawrence A. Johnson, former classical music critic of the Miami Herald, who edits it and its sister Classical Review sites. Its critics include George Grella, who also writes for The Wire and Downbeat. It is a specialist multi-contributor site with an experienced editor whose coverage in our data is opera, which fits T3. Keep.

name: Off Off Online
justification: Off Off Online is a New York review site for off-off-Broadway edited by Edward Karam (Drama Desk board and treasurer) with associate editor Colin Macdonald (Drama Desk voter). Its about page names Drama Desk president Charles Wright and Drama Desk voters Stan Friedman and James Wilson among its writers, and the OCC roster lists OffOffOnline as an affiliation for Deirdre Donovan, Marc Miller and David Schultz. An edited multi-contributor specialist site with recognized critics is T3, not a T4 hobby blog. T2 is not proposed because it is a niche site with no stated pay and a two-tier jump would need more. Move NYC 4 to 3; no London reviews.

name: The Cultural Critic
justification: The Cultural Critic is a US review site covering theater, music, books, art and travel, still active with touring-show reviews in Philadelphia. No about page or masthead could be found, so its owner and editorial model are unverified, and its 6 reviews (2016-2017) are too few for the signals to count. Keep and note it is unverified.

name: The Clyde Fitch Report
justification: The Clyde Fitch Report is an arts and politics website founded in 2006 by Leonard Jacobs, a former Back Stage writer and longtime Drama Desk member, who serves as executive editor. Its reviews in our data come from David Finkle, who also reviews for New York Stage Review and HuffPost, and Martha Wade Steketee. A multi-contributor specialist site with an editor fits T3. Keep.

name: Simon Parris Man In Chair
justification: Man in Chair is the single-author, ad-free blog of Melbourne theatre reviewer Simon Parris, with occasional Broadway reviews from visits. He reviewed for Theatre People for eight years and for the Sunday Herald Sun for two years. No critics' body membership is listed. Borderline T3/T4, but the past newspaper reviewing is some professional standing, so keep T3.

name: Diandra Reviews It All
justification: Diandra Reviews It All is a first-person single-author site run by Diandra Rivera, a singer, actress and freelance writer, covering film and theatre. Her listed memberships (LEJA, NYFCO, WFCO) are film and entertainment journalist groups, not theatre critics' bodies, and the site has no aggregator pickup; its 5 reviews (2017-2018) ran very kind (bias +18). That matches T4; propose nyc3 to nyc4.

name: Magical Misstari Tour
justification: Magical Misstari Tour is a personal Blogger site by Tari Stratton with first-person, fan-style theatre posts (2016-2018). It has no editor, no recognized-critic status was found and there is no aggregator pickup. This is a single-author hobby blog, which matches T4, so a move from T3 is proposed.

name: Adventuresintheatreland
justification: Adventures in Theatreland is a London theatre blog with reviews, interviews and social media accounts, written by several contributors who disclose 'gifted tickets in return for an honest review'. The site publishes no about or team page, so its owner and editorial model could not be confirmed. Its reviews are kind (bias +12.4) but the sample is under 15. The evidence leans toward T4, but it is not enough to move; keep and recheck.

name: Showbiz411
justification: Showbiz411 is an independent entertainment news site co-founded and edited by Roger Friedman, who created the Fox411 column and was later a Hollywood Reporter correspondent. It has a Theater section among Hollywood, music and celebrity coverage, and takes contributors. Friedman is an entertainment columnist rather than a recognized theatre critic, and its consensus gap is high (15.2), but it has an editor and regular Broadway coverage. Keep T3.

name: WNYC
justification: WNYC is New York's public radio station; its theatre reviews (2016-2019) were by Jennifer Vanasco, then WNYC's culture editor and theater critic and an award-winning arts reporter. Vanasco was earlier a theatre critic for the Chicago Reader, is on the faculty of the O'Neill Theater Center National Critics Institute, and later became a senior culture editor at NPR. A paid staff critic at an established outlet fits T2; Show Score data is too thin to use (2 eligible); the consensus gap (10.7) and bias (+0.2) match the reference range. Keep.

name: Flipsidereviews
justification: The Flip Side is a Blogspot blog written by Kevin Filipski covering film, home video, music and some theatre. It is single-author, theatre is a side topic, and no critics'-body membership was found. That fits T4; move 3 to 4. Only 5 reviews.

name: Theater In The Now
justification: Theater In The Now is a blog run by Michael Block, who wrote every visible post; it has no about section and the latest post seen is April 2023. A team page is linked but could not be confirmed. A single-author blog without recognition fits T4; move 3 to 4. Only 6 reviews.

name: Afridiziak Theatre News
justification: Afridiziak Theatre News is a London site celebrating African-Caribbean theatre, set up in 2008 by Sophia A Jackson, who runs it with a family member as web developer and a group of contributors. Its About page says it has supported major theatres 'in the promotion and marketing of their productions', and its scores run far above established critics (bias +12.7). No recognized critics found. Its promotional role and small scale support keeping T4.

name: Broadway Journal
justification: Broadway Journal covers the business of Broadway; its editor Philip Boroff covered culture and finance for Bloomberg News, and Jeremy Gerard (a New York Drama Critics' Circle member) is consulting editor. It is cited by the NYT, Playbill and others for business reporting, while reviews are occasional (8 rows, 2018 to 2019). A small professional specialist outlet fits T3; keep.

name: Bachtrack
justification: Bachtrack is a UK-based site (Bachtrack Ltd, founded January 2008) for classical music, opera and dance, with about 150 reviewers worldwide and specialist editors in four languages. Its rows in our data are opera and dance reviews, so its theatre coverage is incidental, but it is a multi-contributor specialist site with editors. Keep T3; only 11 reviews and consensus data below threshold.

name: Fringereview
justification: FringeReview is a UK review site founded in 2006 by writer Paul Levy, who edits it, covering the Edinburgh and Brighton fringes and, through FringeReview UK, London theatre. It has a multi-reviewer team that accepts applications from new reviewers and is funded partly by reader donations. Our London reviews are almost all by Simon Jenner, a poet and playwright with no critics' body membership found, and they run much kinder than consensus (gap and bias +17.9 on 16 shows).
