A multi-contributor specialist site with a named editor fits T3; the high bias is a caution but not enough to move. Keep.

name: Londonlivinglarge
justification: London Living Large calls itself The City Life Magazine and publishes star-rated reviews of London theatre, exhibitions and events with no bylines, no named editor or writers, and an event-promotion contact link. Our 10 reviews are credited to the site itself and run kind (bias +7.7). With no named critic, no editor and no outside recognition found, it matches the T4 description of a very small site better than T3. Move London 3 to 4 (no NYC reviews; moved with it). Kept: low confidence after research, so the default keep applies.

name: City A.M.
justification: City A.M. is a free London business daily founded in 2005, owned by THG Ingenuity, with ABC circulation of about 68,000 (January 2026) and an editor-in-chief. Theatre is a small part of its arts pages, reviewed by staff writers such as Adam Bloodworth and Steve Dinneen. A professional regional/business paper with incidental theatre coverage fits T3. KEEP.

name: Radio Times
justification: Radio Times is a UK national listings magazine founded in 1923 and published by Immediate Media, focused on TV and radio; theatre reviews appear in a Going Out section. The reviewers in our data (Olivia Garrett, Joanna Magill) could not be identified as established critics, and the site blocked direct fetch. Bias is +9.8 with a gap of 15.6, kinder than established critics. Not enough verified to move; keep T3.

name: South London
justification: southlondon.co.uk is published by Community Matters Media Ltd, whose print titles include South London Weekly, Southwark News and the Greenwich & Lewisham Weekender; Southwark News was founded in 1987 and is described as the only independent paid-for newspaper in London, with a named editor. Theatre reviews run under Lifestyle & Events with no star ratings; the sampled review is bylined Michael Holland through what appears to be a staff-reporter account, while its text credits Leo Dunlop, so the single-critic attribution in our data is uncertain. No critics' body membership or aggregator pickup was found. A local newspaper group with regular theatre reviewing matches the T3 definition (local or regional papers), not T4, so lon4 to lon3 is confirmed.

name: Aleks Sierz
justification: sierz.co.uk is the personal review site of Aleks Sierz, a member of the UK Critics' Circle, Fellow of the RSA and author of In-Yer-Face Theatre (Faber, 2001) and several Methuen Drama books on British theatre, who teaches for Boston University's London Programme. It is single-author, but the author is a recognized critic and scholar, which takes it out of T4. Keep T3. Our rows carry no critic names for it (data artifact).

name: Theartsdispatch
justification: The Arts Dispatch is a Substack publication of theatre and arts reviews launched in 2026; reviews are credited only to the publication and its About page names no writer, editor or credentials. Its few scores sit close to consensus (gap 4.1 over 9 reviews, below threshold). An anonymous newsletter would usually fit T4, but nothing could be verified either way, so per the rules keep T3 and flag as unverified.

name: Upstage Downstage
justification: Upstage-Downstage is Howard Miller's blog. He is the lead Broadway critic at Talkin' Broadway, a member of ATCA and a voting member of the Outer Critics Circle and Drama Desk, so the single-author blog carries recognized-critic status. Keep T3.

name: Film Festival Traveler
justification: Film Festival Traveler describes itself as the traveler's resource guide to festivals and films, part of Insider Media LLC's Festival Travel Network; its sections cover film festivals, expos, gadgets and travel, with theatre as an occasional item. Our 11 reviews (2015-2017) are all by Kevin Filipski, with no critics' body membership found. Theatre coverage is incidental to a film-festival site with no aggregator pickup, which is the T4 definition, even though its scores track consensus (gap 6.9). Move NYC 3 to 4.

name: Slant Magazine
justification: Slant Magazine is a US online culture publication co-founded in 2001 by Ed Gonzalez, who is its film editor and a New York Film Critics Circle member, and it covers film, music, TV and theater. Its theater reviews are mostly by Dan Rubins, who sits on the Outer Critics Circle board and lists TheaterMania, Slant, Brooklyn Rail and The Present Stage; a second OCC board member, Gerard Raymond, also lists Slant. Its consensus gap (10.6) and bias (-1.7) are within the reference range. An edited, long-running professional outlet whose theater critics hold recognized standing fits T2; keep.

name: Li Herald
justification: LI Herald (liherald.com) is a Long Island local newspaper site; our five reviews from 2017 are by Elyse Trevers, who has 40 reviews at StageBuddy in our data. The site blocked fetching (403) and web search budget was exhausted, so ownership and editorial details could not be verified. A local paper fits T3 by definition; keep.

name: Susangranger.com
justification: Susangranger.com is the personal site of Susan Granger, a film critic and broadcast commentator for over 40 years whose reviews are syndicated by SSG Syndicate. Her listed memberships are film bodies (Critics Choice Association, Online Film Critics Society, New York Film Critics Online, AWFJ), not theater ones. Single-author, mainly film, but she is a recognized professional critic; with only 5 reviews, KEEP nyc3.

name: Newsweek
justification: Newsweek is a US national news magazine, but its theater reviews in our data (2016-2022) were written mainly by Joe Westerfield, whose byline lists him as a copy editor, not a critic. Theater coverage there is incidental and no aggregator pickup was found, which points toward T4, but a national magazine with an editorial process sits at least at T3. KEEP nyc3 with low confidence; a T4 case exists.

name: Hampstead & Highgate Express
justification: The Ham & High is a weekly paid local newspaper in Camden, north London, now owned by Newsquest after Archant. Its reviewer Bridget Galton has been its features editor. A local paper with staff reviewers fits T3. Keep.

name: DC Metro Theater Arts
justification: DC Metro Theater Arts (now DC Theater Arts) is a Washington-area theatre site founded by Joel Markowitz, with a named editor-in-chief since 2017 and many writers covering everything from tours to community productions. Markowitz asked writers to always find something positive in a production, consistent with its kind scores (bias +7.0 on 8 shows). Multi-contributor with an editor fits T3; keep. Note our data also has a separate dc-theater-arts id for the same publication.

name: Theatre is Easy
justification: Theatre is Easy (Theasy) is a New York theatre review website founded in 2007 as a blog by Molly Marinik to cover Off and Off-Off Broadway; it grew into a multi-contributor site whose reviews are written by theatre practitioners. Its team included Dan Dinero, described as a Drama Desk voting member, and Dan Rubins, who later reviewed for Slant and TheaterMania. That is a multi-contributor specialist site with an editor, which fits T3. Keep.

name: Cabaret Scenes
justification: Cabaret Scenes is a cabaret-focused publication whose Broadway reviews here (17, 2016 to 2025) are mostly by Elizabeth Ahlfors. The site returned 403 to every request and the web search budget ran out, so its editorial model and the critic's standing could not be verified. A niche specialist magazine fits T3 on its face; keep.

name: The Cleveland Plain Dealer
justification: The Plain Dealer is Cleveland's main daily, owned by Advance Publications; since 2020 its content is produced by cleveland.com, where most of these reviews (Joey Morona, Playhouse Square tours) appear. The id also holds at least one review from a different outlet, a Star 102 Cleveland radio post on audacy.com, so it mixes two publications. A regional daily fits T3. KEEP, and split out the audacy.com row.

name: 4Columns
justification: 4Columns is an edited arts-criticism website that publishes four thousand-word reviews a week and states that it compensates its contributors fairly. Its theater reviews here are by Helen Shaw (also NYT, Vulture, The New Yorker) and David Cote (New York Drama Critics' Circle member), so every critic is established. Paid, edited criticism by recognized critics matches T2 rather than T3; propose nyc2. The site navigation now shows 'The End of 4Columns', so it may have closed; standing while active still applies.

name: theatreboard
justification: The sample URLs are paged discussion threads (theatreboard.com/thread/ID/show-name?page=N) and the row has zero named critics, which indicates these entries are posts from a theatregoers' message board rather than critic reviews. The site blocked fetching (406), so this could not be confirmed directly. This looks like a data artifact; keep the tier per the brief, and flag the rows for removal from scoring rather than re-tiering.

name: Rolandcat Reviews
justification: Rolandcat Reviews ('Roviews') is a personal Substack of 'Theatre, opera and Comedy Reviews' by an author named only as Roland, started in 2026. It is a single-author blog with no editor and no recognized-critic status, and its scores run well above established critics (bias +10.7 on 8 reviews). T4 fits. Keep.

name: Cote Notices
justification: Cote Notices is David Cote's Substack newsletter. It is single-author, but Cote was the longest-serving theater editor and chief drama critic of Time Out New York and has written for the Observer, 4Columns and American Theatre, which is clear recognized-critic status. Keep T3.

name: Fairy Powered Productions
justification: Fairy Powered Productions is a UK blog ('We are watching you...') that mixes reposted press announcements with reviews by a few bylined writers; it names no owner, editor or team. Its reviews run very kind (bias +15.9, small sample). A hobby blog with no aggregator pickup fits T4; keep.

name: Pinkprincetheatre
justification: Pink Prince Theatre is a Wix site that calls itself a theatre lovers website; every review is by Neill Kovacic-Clarke, written in the first person, with no editor or credentials shown. A single-author fan site with no recognition fits T4; move London 3 to 4 (no NYC reviews, aligned to 4). Only 8 reviews, all in 2026.

name: Unmissabletheatre
justification: Unmissable Theatre is a London theatre review site run by Megan, a Londoner and occasional amateur performer who describes herself as the voice behind the site and appears to be its only writer; it also carries ticket-buying pages. A single-author blog with no editor, no recognized-critic status and no aggregator pickup is the T4 definition. Move London 3 to 4 (no NYC reviews; moved with it).

name: Theater Reviews from My Seat
justification: Theater Reviews from My Seat appears to be a single-author blog by Joe Lombardi (10 rows, 2018 to 2019). The site returned an empty page and the web search budget ran out, so nothing could be verified. Its consensus numbers are ordinary. Keep and note as a possible T4 candidate.

name: National Review
justification: National Review is a US national political magazine; its six Broadway reviews (2018-2019) are by Kyle Smith, then its critic-at-large, a former New York Post film critic who is now a Wall Street Journal film critic and theatre critic for The New Criterion. The critic is established, but theatre is incidental to a political magazine, the sample is tiny and its scores run far below consensus (bias -16.9, n=6). Those facts pull in opposite directions; keep.

name: Rolling Stone
justification: Rolling Stone is a US national monthly magazine on music, politics and entertainment owned by Penske Media. Theater is incidental to its coverage: 21 reviews over 14 years by 9 writers, mostly music and film writers, and only 2 of them also review regularly at T1/T2 outlets. A national publication with editors fits T2 on standing even though it is not a theater authority; with no clear evidence for a different tier and a small sample (bias +7.4, n=21), keep.

name: Towncountry
justification: Town & Country is a Hearst monthly lifestyle magazine founded in 1846 with circulation near 486,000 (2015). Its few theater reviews (2016-2017) were written mainly by Jesse Oxfeld, who has 31 reviews at New York Stage Review in our data. A national niche magazine with occasional theater coverage fits T3. KEEP.

name: The Spectator (UK)
justification: The Spectator is a long-running UK national weekly magazine; all 52 rows are by Lloyd Evans, its theatre critic and parliamentary sketch-writer. It is much harsher than consensus (bias -10.5, gap 17.0), which reflects one critic's voice rather than standing. A national weekly with a regular paid critic fits T2; keep.

name: Medium
justification: Medium is a self-publishing platform, not a publication, so this id is a data artifact that groups personal blogs. 17 of its 20 rows come from Christian Lewis's own Medium blog; Lewis is an Outer Critics Circle member listed as a freelancer for TheaterMania, Variety and Theatrely, and the one-off rows include David Cote and Kyle Turner. There is no editorial layer, but the main author is a recognized critic, so per the data-artifact rule keep the current tier and consider re-attributing the rows to the individual critic.

name: Peconic Public Broadcasting
justification: Peconic Public Broadcasting owned WPPB, the NPR member station on Long Island, from 2010 until its sale to The WNET Group in 2020 (now WLIW-FM). Its reviews in our data (2015-2018) are by David Richardson, presented as the station's theatre critic. A local public radio station with a regular critic fits T3; as a defunct outlet it keeps that standing. Could not verify Richardson's critics' body membership. Keep.

name: Nytheatre
justification: nytheatre.com was the indie-theatre review site run by Martin Denton through the nonprofit New York Theatre Experience, which ended in 2017; it used volunteer reviewer teams alongside Denton. That is a multi-contributor specialist site with an editor, matching T3, so keep. Note the row's domain is nytheatre-wire.com while sample URLs are nytheatre.com, which may mix two different sites.

name: Chicago Sun-Times
justification: The Chicago Sun-Times is a major metropolitan daily founded in 1948, owned since 2022 by Chicago Public Media, with about 57,000 print copies and a professional newsroom. It has sustained theater criticism (Hedy Weiss covered theater for it from 1984 to 2017) and reviews Chicago productions and tours. A big-city daily with an ongoing critic role fits T2 for US regional reviews. KEEP.

name: Parterre Box
justification: Parterre Box is an opera magazine founded as a zine in 1993 by critic James Jorden, now a website with an international roster of contributors, a newsletter and advertising; it quotes the New York Times calling it 'the most essential blog in opera'. Theatre is a side interest (15 rows). A niche specialist magazine with recognition in its own field fits T3; keep.

name: Onin
justification: Onin (ON IN LONDON) is a small online lifestyle magazine 'by real Londoners' covering arts, business, health, fashion, food, travel and more, run by its editor/owner Tegan LeBon with one other named writer, Caitlin Neal, who wrote all its theatre reviews. Theatre is incidental to a very small general-lifestyle site, its reviewer has no recognized-critic status found, and it has no aggregator pickup. That fits T4; propose lon3 to lon4.

name: Viewfromthegods
justification: View from the Gods is a single-author review blog by Simon Jenner, a poet and playwright who also reviews for FringeReview; no editor or other reviewers appear and the oldest visible post is January 2024. No critics'-body membership was found for Jenner. A single-author blog without recognized-critic status fits T4; move London 3 to 4 (no NYC reviews, aligned to 4). Only 7 reviews.

name: Vox
justification: Vox is a US explanatory-journalism news site founded in 2014 and now owned by Lupa Systems. Its 9 theater reviews over six years were written by staff culture writers (Constance Grady, a senior correspondent who previously ran book coverage, and Aja Romano), not a theater critic. Vox is a professional national outlet but lacks the sustained theatre coverage and recognized theater critic the T2 definition requires; T3 fits better. Move nyc2 to nyc3.

name: Adriandimanlig
justification: This is Adrian Dimanlig's personal arts blog (Interludes), with reviews posted as 'The Hangover Report'. It is single-author, but Dimanlig states he is a member of the American Theatre Critics Association and the International Association of Theatre Critics, has served on the Joseph Jefferson Awards Committee and is a Drama Desk nominator. That recognized-critic status keeps it at T3. KEEP.

name: This Broadway
justification: This Broadway (thisbroadsway.com) appears to be a single-author blog by Sandra McFarland (6 rows, 2014 to 2018) that runs kind (+11.8, tiny sample). The site refused connections and the web search budget ran out, so nothing could be verified. Keep and note as a T4 candidate.

name: The Interested Bystander
justification: The Interested Bystander is Cary Wong's single-author blog. Wong is a reviewer and columnist for Film Score Monthly and writes cabaret reviews for BroadwayWorld, but I found no theatre critics' body membership. This is borderline between T3 and T4; with paid outside writing and not enough evidence to move, keep T3.

name: Pioneer Press
justification: The St. Paul Pioneer Press (twincities.com) is a Minnesota daily newspaper; its reviews here are of touring productions by Rob Hubbard and Ross Raihala. A regional daily reviewing tours fits T3 by definition; keep. Critic credentials were not verified.

name: Pop Dust
justification: Popdust describes itself as a source of 'informed opinions on pop culture, music, movies, TV, celebrity news, internet trends, and entertainment', and its front page now carries sponsored product posts. Its 5 Broadway reviews (2017 to 2018, one writer) are incidental to that coverage, and no critic standing was found. An outlet whose theatre coverage is incidental fits T4; propose nyc4.

name: Theatre Vibe
justification: TheatreVibe is a small London review site launched in 2020 as the outlet for Lizzie Loveridge, with Reece George credited for building it and no named editor. Its about page says Loveridge was a member of the Critics' Circle, began reviewing in the mid-1990s and joined CurtainUp as its London critic in January 2000; a 2021 West End Frame page independently describes her as a Critics' Circle member and CurtainUp's Chief London Critic. The case against the move is that this is effectively one critic's personal site with no aggregator pickup found and membership stated in the past tense. But T4 excludes writers with recognized-critic status, and a 25-year London critic with Critics' Circle membership has it, so lon4 to lon3 is confirmed.

name: TIME
justification: TIME is a national news magazine; its theatre reviews here are mostly by Richard Zoglin, a TIME staff writer and editor for more than 30 years who served as its theatre critic. Our data ends in 2014. A national magazine with a staff critic fits at least T2; theatre coverage was occasional, so no case for T1. Keep.

name: The Three Tomatoes
justification: The Three Tomatoes is a lifestyle magazine and newsletter for midlife women founded by Cheryl Benton, covering fashion, travel, food and health; theatre reviews are an incidental part. Its 5 reviews are by one writer with no recognized-critic status found. Incidental theatre coverage matches T4, so move from T3.

name: PicksInSix
justification: PicksInSix is the short-form review section of Conversations with Ed Tracy, a Chicago and Midwest site run by Ed Tracy through Roxbury Road Creative with a group of contributing writers, now ten years old. It credits ATCA and Theatre in Chicago for placing reviews. Small multi-contributor specialist site; keep T3 with low confidence.

name: timesofsandiego
justification: Times of San Diego is a nonprofit local news site covering San Diego County, with a newsroom covering arts among other beats; it says its staff has won nearly 200 awards and it holds NewsGuard and Journalism Trust Initiative certification. Its theatre reviews (touring shows) come from Drew Sitton. A professional local news outlet fits T3. Keep.

name: Operawire
justification: OperaWire is an opera news, features and review website with David Salazar as editor-in-chief and Francisco Salazar as publisher, and a team of contributors that it invites readers to join. Its reviews in our data are Metropolitan Opera productions. It is a specialist multi-contributor site with an editor, which fits T3. Keep.

name: Josh at the Movies
justification: Josh at the Movies is a WordPress.com film blog that also covers television and theater, with two Josh contributors and no editor shown. Theatre coverage is incidental (12 rows) and reviews run far kinder than consensus (bias +15.8, small sample). This is a hobby blog with incidental theatre coverage; keep T4.

name: Rhombus Rota
justification: Rhombus Rota is a UK theatre site with the tagline Applauding The Arts, covering local and amateur as well as professional theatre. It names no editor or team, and searches found nothing else about it. That points toward T4, but with only 6 reviews and nothing verified about who runs it, keep T3 and flag for recheck.

name: San Diego Union-Tribune
justification: The San Diego Union-Tribune is a regional daily; its reviews here are by Pam Kragen, its theatre and food critic and a former president of the San Diego Theatre Critics Circle. A regional paper with a recognized local critic fits T3; keep.

name: Dallasvoice
justification: Dallas Voice is the LGBTQ newspaper of North Texas, published for four decades by Voice Publishing Company, Inc., with a weekly print PDF edition, news, arts and a theater reviews section. A regional weekly paper with an arts section fits T3; keep.

name: London Theatre Reviews
justification: London Theatre Reviews (LTR) is a small UK review site with no About page, no named editor or operator, and homepage listings with no bylines. Reviews are headed 'by LTR' with a closing reviewer credit (for example Sunita Jaswal, Emma Foxhall), under a shared bio reading 'Last year I attended more than 100 shows in London', which describes an enthusiast writer rather than a professional critic. No critics' body membership, no aggregator pickup and no press coverage of the site turned up; Matt Wolf is not credited on the sampled pages. That is the T4 profile, so the London move from 3 to 4 stands (NYC unused, aligned).

name: Metro UK
justification: Metro is a British free tabloid newspaper published by DMG Media, which became the most-circulated UK newspaper in 2018; theatre reviews are occasional. Its sampleUrls include a theatrevibe.co.uk link, so this id mixes in at least one review from a different site. A mass-market national paper with incidental theatre coverage and occasional established freelancers (Claire Allfree) fits T3. Keep.

name: Buffalo Rising
justification: Buffalo Rising is an online magazine founded in 2003 by Newell Nussbaumer, focused on hyperlocal Buffalo coverage; its theatre reviews in our data are touring shows at Shea's. It is a local multi-writer publication, which fits T3. Keep.

name: Lost in Theatreland
justification: Lost in Theatreland is a WordPress theatre blog covering London and Edinburgh shows with news and ticket tips. It names no owner or editor on its home page, and has a small team page. This fits T4. Keep.

name: Express  (UK)
justification: The Daily Express is a UK national middle-market daily owned by Reach plc, circulation 102,884 (December 2025), editor Geoff Maynard since September 2025. Its theatre reviewer Neil Norman joined the Evening Standard in 1986 as a film critic and has reviewed theatre for the Express from at least 2014 to 2024 and for The Stage as recently as May 2026, and the Express is quoted among national papers in a London Theatre Direct press-quote page. The argument for going higher (T2) is the national masthead and a long-serving critic, but its theatre coverage in our data is thin (18 reviews over 27 years, several by entertainment writers) and runs kind (+6.5). A national paper with a professional critic is not T4; T3 is confirmed.

name: About Entertainment (theater.about.com — defunct)
justification: This id is the theater section of About.com, a commercial network of topic guides that IAC retired and rebranded as Dotdash in 2017, so the outlet is defunct. Both reviews are by its guide Chris Caggiano. Only 2 reviews exist, so impact is negligible and there is no basis to move; keep.

name: Albany Times-Union
justification: The Times Union is Albany's daily broadsheet newspaper, founded in 1856 and owned by Hearst, covering New York's Capital Region (66,835 daily circulation in 2011). Our reviews are of touring shows at Proctors by Katherine Kiessling. A regional daily paper reviewing tours fits T3; keep.

name: Aaron in NYC
justification: Aaron in NYC is a first-person personal review site covering NYC theatre and comedy, with no named full author, editor or other contributors. A single-author personal blog with no recognition fits T4; move 3 to 4. Only 6 reviews.

name: Partially Obstructed View
justification: Partially Obstructed View is a personal Blogspot blog whose tagline is 'Writing down what I think about theatre I've seen in That London, whether I've been asked to or not', with posts by a single user ('nick730'). It is a single-author hobby blog with no aggregator pickup or recognized-critic status found, which is the T4 definition; propose lon3 to lon4. The critic name 'View my Complete' in our data is a scraping artifact from the Blogger profile link.

name: Cultural Capital
justification: Cultural Capital is Maryam Philpott's personal WordPress blog. It is single-author, but Philpott is a Critics' Circle member, has been a London theatre critic for The Reviews Hub since 2014, and wrote a book on James Graham shortlisted for the Society for Theatre Research Book Prize 2025. Recognized-critic status keeps it out of T4; keep T3.

name: ReviewsGate
justification: ReviewsGate is a UK arts reviews website covering theatre, music, dance and film, reviewing since 2001 per its About page. Its Our Reviewers page names a Co-Founder and Editor (Roderick Dungate), a Deputy Editor for reviews (William Russell, former London Editor and film critic of the Glasgow Herald and former Hon Gen Secretary of the Critics' Circle) and about ten named reviewers. The Critics' Circle drama page lists William Russell as an honorary member and Rod Dungate and Clare Colvin as members. A multi-contributor specialist site with a named editor and Critics' Circle critics does not fit the T4 definition and matches T3, so move one tier; only 5 reviews and a +7.4 bias on 5 shows keep confidence at medium.

name: Seatplan
justification: SeatPlan is a UK and New York theatre ticketing and seat-view site: its review pages carry ticket links, a basket and an 'Official Ticket Guarantee', and its content is driven by members who earn rewards for reviews and seat photos. Review bylines link to member profiles, and the sampled review names two different authors. A ticket seller reviewing shows it sells is promotional, and all 5 of its scored reviews sit far above the established critics (bias +17.9). Move lon3 to lon4 (nyc3 to nyc4).

name: Revstanstheatreblog
justification: Rev Stan's Theatre Blog is a personal London theatre blog: its author (Stacey) says she set it up in 2010 'primarily to keep a record of everything I'd seen', that it 'doesn't make me money, and I don't get paid', and that she works by day as a business writer. That is the T4 description (single-author hobby blog) and no aggregator pickup or critics' body membership was found. Propose lon4.

name: The Morning Star
justification: The Morning Star is a UK national daily owned by a reader co-operative, the People's Press Printing Society, with theatre reviews by named reviewers. A small national paper with regular arts reviews fits T3; its 5 reviews here run kind but the sample is too small to judge. Keep.

name: Harry Theatre Life
justification: Harry Theatre Life is a personal Wix theatre blog by Harry Brogan ('I'm Harry the Theatre Kid ... and have begun my journey into Theatre blogging'), with affiliate ticket links. It is a single-author hobby blog with no editor and no recognized-critic status. This matches T4, so a move from T3 is proposed.

name: UInterview
justification: uInterview is a celebrity news and video interview site with sister sites for sports, politics and travel, which also promotes concert ticket deals. Its 5 theatre reviews (2014-2019) are incidental to that coverage, and I found no critic credentials for the writers. That matches T4, so move NYC and London from T3 to T4.

name: IndieWire
justification: IndieWire is a film and TV news and criticism site owned by Penske Media, which also owns Variety. Its 2 reviews here are by its film critic David Ehrlich, so theatre is incidental. With only 2 reviews and an established professional publisher, there is not enough to justify a move; keep.

name: San Jose Mercury News
justification: The Mercury News is a San Jose daily owned by Digital First Media (Alden Global Capital) and published by the Bay Area News Group, with about 24,000 daily print and 150,000 Sunday circulation. A regional daily fits T3; keep.

name: New York Notebook
justification: New York Notebook is a Substack newsletter by Sandy MacDonald, describing itself as a guide to theatre worth seeing and other New York City enticements. It is a single-author newsletter, but our data shows MacDonald also has 11 reviews at New York Stage Review and others at TheaterMania and Time Out, so she has some standing as a working critic; her full credentials could not be verified. Not enough to justify a move; keep.

name: New City Stage
justification: Newcity Stage is the performing arts section of Newcity, a Chicago arts and culture publication from Newcity Communications. It covers theater, dance and comedy in Chicago, with several bylined writers; its reviews in our data are of Broadway tours in Chicago. A local arts publication fits T3. Keep.

name: Flicker Magazine
justification: Flicker Magazine is a queer-led independent online magazine (Lexme Media Group, ISSN 2979-3165) covering LGBTQ theatre, film and culture from London. It has a masthead with a founder, an editor-in-chief and a senior editor plus a dozen writers and contributors; pay status is not stated. A multi-contributor niche magazine with editors fits T3. Its 7 reviews are too few to read the bias. KEEP.

name: Boston Globe
justification: The Boston Globe is a major metropolitan daily whose theatre critic, Don Aucoin, is a staff writer and Nieman Fellow. Its reviews in our data are mostly of touring and pre-Broadway productions in Boston. As a regional paper with a staff critic it fits T3 by definition, though a case for T2 exists similar to other big-city dailies; the evidence is not clear enough to move, so keep.

name: Londontheatredirect
justification: London Theatre Direct is a ticket seller that calls itself 'one of the leading providers of theatre tickets in the UK'; its reviews sit in a news section, carry no star rating, and link to the reviewed show's ticket page with Book Tickets buttons and prices. The sampled reviews are by Hay Brunsdon, whose bio cites West End industry work since 2012 rather than critic standing, and no editor or critics' body membership was found. Its reviews average 20.8 points kinder than established critics on the same 16 shows, consistent with promotional writing. A seller's marketing reviews fit T4, so lon3 to lon4 is confirmed.

name: Edge New York
justification: Edge New York is the New York edition of EDGE Media Network, an LGBTQ online news and entertainment network (identified from the review URLs). Its site and Wikipedia page could not be fetched, so ownership and editorial model are unverified. Its 6 reviews (all dated the same day, likely an import artifact) are too few to read the bias. KEEP nyc3 and note what could not be verified.

name: Maryland Theatre Guide
justification: MD Theatre Guide is a Maryland theatre website founded by theatre professional Mark Beachy, owned by MD Theatre Guide LLC, with several reviewers. A regional multi-contributor specialist site fits T3; I could not verify editor or pay details, so keep.

name: Minneapolis Star Tribune
justification: The Star Tribune is the Minneapolis daily newspaper (about 110,000 digital subscribers, 54,800 average print), owned by Glen Taylor, with eight Pulitzer Prizes. Most reviews here are by Rohan Preston, whose role could not be confirmed because the site rate-limited fetches. A major regional paper fits T3 (local or regional papers); keep. Only 5 reviews.

name: Thelivereview
justification: The Live Review (thelivereview.co.uk) has 6 London rows, all by Tanya Howard, every one far kinder than consensus (+23.1, tiny sample). The site returned 403 and the search budget ran out, so its model could not be checked. Keep and note as a T4 candidate.

name: The News Herald
justification: The News-Herald is a local daily newspaper; its 6 reviews are by Mark Meszoros of touring shows at Playhouse Square in Cleveland. I could not fetch the site to verify ownership or the writer's role, and my search budget ran out. A local paper fits T3; keep.

name: Matinee Mouse
justification: Matinee Mouse is a UK Substack-based arts publication established in 2023 that 'began as a passion project', focuses on accessible culture, includes ticket offers in reviews and says it collaborates with producers and marketing professionals on bespoke campaigns. It reports about 195K combined monthly views. No recognized critics or editor named, and it has 6 reviews in our data. T4 fits. Keep.

name: The Knockturnal
justification: The Knockturnal is an entertainment and lifestyle site describing itself as a collective of fashion, music and entertainment industry insiders, with sections for entertainment, music, lifestyle, automotive and fashion. Theatre coverage is incidental, no editor is named, and its contributors have no found critic credentials. That matches T4, so move NYC and London from T3 to T4.

name: Metrmag
justification: METRMag (Massachusetts Entertainment & Theatre Review Magazine) is a web magazine whose publisher and primary reviewer, Kevin T. Baldwin, is a member of the American Theatre Critics Association and has reviewed theatre for the Worcester Telegram & Gazette since 2011. Essentially single-author, but by a recognized critic, so T3 rather than T4; keep. Two critic name variants in our data are the same person.

name: JK's Theatre Scene
justification: JK's Theatre Scene is a personal theatre-fan blog by 'JK', a self-described major theatre enthusiast, mixing trivia games and reviews and noting the views are the author's own. Single author, no editor, no recognized-critic status found. Keep T4.

name: OC Register
justification: The Orange County Register is a paid daily newspaper in California, founded in 1905 and owned by Alden Global Capital; its reviews in our data cover touring productions at Segerstrom Center. A regional paper with a regular reviewer fits T3. Keep. Reviewer credentials were not verified.

name: West End Wilma
justification: West End Wilma is a London theatre blog created by Ed Baker and his mother under the Wilma persona, which recruits writers to review UK shows. No editor is named and no critics' body membership is mentioned. This matches T4. Keep.

name: clevescene
justification: Cleveland Scene is an alternative weekly newspaper founded in 1970, covering local arts, music, dining and film, owned by Great Lakes Publishing since 2024. Our five reviews are touring shows at Playhouse Square by Gwendolyn Kocher. A local paper reviewing tours fits T3; keep.

name: The Culture Mom
justification: The Culture Mom is Holly Rosen Fink's single-author culture and parenting site (2016-2018 reviews in our data). Its about page and home page returned empty, and the Wayback Machine could not be reached, so its editorial model and the author's credentials are unverified. It looks like a T4 candidate, but I could not verify enough to move it. KEEP nyc3.

name: Hollywood Soapbox
justification: Hollywood Soapbox's site returned 401 to fetching, so its ownership and editorial model could not be verified. All three reviews are by John Soltes and run far kinder than consensus (bias +15.4, n=3, too few to rely on). With nothing verified that supports a higher tier, keep T4.

name: Mashable
justification: Mashable is a national news and entertainment website founded in 2005. Its theatre reviews in our data come mainly from Erin Strecker, who is on the 2026-27 Outer Critics Circle roster with a Mashable affiliation. Theatre is an occasional beat for a large general site, which fits T3 rather than T2. Keep.

name: The Arts Fuse
justification: The Arts Fuse is an independent online arts magazine for Boston and New England, founded in 2007, edited by Bill Marx, and published by the 501(c)(3) nonprofit Global Narratives. It has over 70 freelance critics. A regional specialist magazine with an editor fits T3. Keep.

name: Chicago Reader
justification: The Chicago Reader is Chicago's alternative newspaper ('Chicago's alternative newsroom'), with a staff page, freelance guidelines and a print edition. Its reviews here are of Chicago productions by freelance and staff critics such as Kerry Reid. A local paper fits T3; keep.

name: The Forward
justification: The Forward is a national American Jewish news outlet; its theatre reviews here are few (14) and mostly by culture writer PJ Grisar, with a couple by Jesse Green and Jesse Oxfeld. I could not open the Forward's author or about pages to verify roles, and theatre coverage is a small part of its output. Without verified facts to support a move, keep T4.

name: Fort Worth Star-Telegram
justification: The Fort Worth Star-Telegram is a McClatchy daily with about 13,000 print and 14,000 digital subscribers. Its 3 reviews in our data are by Rick Mauch, whose role could not be checked because the site blocks fetching. A local daily fits T3. KEEP.

name: The Jitney
justification: The Jitney (jitneybooks.com) is a small Miami-focused news, arts and literary site tied to a small publishing company, funded by reader donations, with J.J. Colagrande writing many of its posts; theatre is one category among movies, TV, politics, music, sports and books. Theatre coverage is incidental to a small local site, which fits T4; keep.

name: Luxury Experience
justification: Luxury Experience is a luxury travel, hotel and dining website; no theatre coverage was visible beyond the single review in our data. Theatre coverage is incidental, which fits T4. Keep.

name: Broadway Select
justification: Broadway Select is a site where Peter Filichia wrote all 17 reviews in our data (2015-2019); the site now fails with a certificate error, so its owner and model could not be checked. Filichia is a long-standing Broadway critic and author who was president of the Drama Desk before David Sheward. A single-author outlet by a recognized critic fits T3 under the definitions; keep.

name: Rachelweinbergreviews
justification: Rachel Weinberg Reviews is a personal blog by a Chicago marketing professional who says she is co-lead editor and chief theater critic of BroadwayWorld's Chicago section. A single-author blog fits T4, but the author has some standing as a regional BroadwayWorld editor, and with 5 rows the evidence is not clear enough to move. Keep.

name: Hartford Courant
justification: The Hartford Courant is a Connecticut daily newspaper founded in 1764, owned by Tribune Publishing (Alden Global Capital), with print circulation of about 19,400. A regional daily reviewing Broadway and touring shows fits T3; keep.

name: 1883magazine
justification: 1883 Magazine is a London culture and fashion magazine; its 5 theatre reviews come from three writers, one of whom (Franco Milazzo) also reviews for BroadwayWorld and Plays International. I could not reach its about page (403), so editorial model is unverified. Keep T3 with low confidence.

name: Blogcritics
justification: Blogcritics is an online magazine founded in 2002, now owned by executive editors Barbara Barnett and Jon Sobel, with an open contributor base and editorial review before publication. Its New York theatre reviews are mostly by Sobel. It has won blog awards and is an accredited Google News source. A multi-contributor site with editors fits T3; keep.

name: The A.V. Club
justification: The A.V. Club is a professional pop-culture site whose theatre coverage is incidental: 3 rows, framed as 'reaction' pieces to stage versions of screen properties, all far kinder than consensus (tiny sample). Incidental theatre coverage fits T4; keep. The search budget ran out before ownership and writer details could be checked.

name: Splash Magazines
justification: Splash Magazines Worldwide is an online lifestyle site founded by Lawrence Davis in 1999 as a hobby, covering varied aspects of life; theatre is one of many topics, spread across six different writers in our 7 reviews. No recognized critics were found and its scores run kind (bias +10.7, small sample). Hobby origin and incidental theatre coverage match T4, so move from T3.

name: Billboard
justification: Billboard is a music industry magazine published by Penske Media; its 5 items in our data come from 5 different writers between 2015 and 2022, and at least one is a cast album review ('Hamilton' cast recording) rather than a stage review. Theatre is incidental to its coverage and it has no theatre critic, so T2 does not fit; a move to T3 is proposed. Some rows may be data artifacts (album or news pieces).

name: Plays To See
justification: Plays To See is a UK review site founded by Rivka Jacobson in 2010 and registered as a charity (No. 1151193), with a mission to explore cultures through the performing arts. It has multiple contributors, published reviewer guidelines and a young reviewers section; its reviewer Wilder Gutterson has a stage directing MA and 20 years as a New York actor and director. Pay status and the current editor were not found. A multi-contributor specialist site fits T3; keep.

name: The Oakland Press
justification: The Oakland Press is a daily newspaper in Oakland County, Michigan, owned by MediaNews Group. Its reviews here are of touring Broadway shows by Gary Graff. A local daily fits T3. Keep.

name: America Magazine
justification: America is a Catholic magazine published by the Jesuits of the United States since 1909. Its theatre reviews in our data are by Rob Weinert-Kendt, whom the magazine identifies as editor of American Theatre magazine and a writer for The New York Times and Time Out New York. The T4 definition requires no recognized-critic status, which does not hold here, so a move to T3 is proposed; theatre is an occasional beat, so not higher.

name: Curtain Call Reviews
justification: Curtain Call Reviews is Emma Rowley's single-author blog, tagline Sharing my love of theatre, covering mainly West Midlands venues plus London. No editor or critic credentials are named. This is a hobby blog and fits T4. Keep.

name: Lbc
justification: LBC is a London talk-radio station that also publishes news online. Its 2 theatre reviews were written by Johnny Jenkins, whose role at LBC the page does not state. Theatre coverage is incidental to a talk-radio outlet with no named critic, which fits T4. KEEP.

name: Around the Town Chicago
justification: Around the Town Chicago is a Chicago-area review site run and signed by Alan Bresloff ('It is my desire to make you aware of all that is going on'), who is the main byline, with no editor named and only occasional other reviewers. A largely single-author site with no aggregator pickup or recognized-critic status found fits T4; its few reviews in our data also run kind (bias +12.3, n=5). Propose nyc3 to nyc4.

name: People
justification: People is a US national weekly celebrity magazine owned by People Inc., with about 2.2 million paid subscribers. All 9 reviews in our data are by Dave Quinn, who also covers theater for NBC New York and EW in our data. Theater is a small part of its coverage and the sample is tiny, but a national edited publication sits at T2 on standing; people.com blocked fetches, so Quinn's title was not verified. Keep.

name: PureWow
justification: PureWow is a lifestyle site covering fashion, beauty, food and travel, operated by Wow Media Products; its Broadway reviews are by entertainment-news writers whose bios do not mention theatre. Theatre is incidental and no recognized critics were found; keep T4.

name: Theatre News
justification: Theatre-News.com is a UK theatre site whose navigation is built around tickets, competitions, comps, guest posts, a 'theatre promo SEO tool', a media pack and sister music, film and game news sites. That points to a promotional site with incidental reviewing (2 rows). Keep T4.

name: The Globe and Mail
justification: The Globe and Mail is Canada's self-described national newspaper, owned by the Thomson family's Woodbridge Company, with weekly readership above 6 million in 2024. Its reviews here are by J. Kelly Nestruck, its staff chief theatre critic from 2008 to 2024. A national daily with a long-serving staff theatre critic fits T2 (established professional outlet), not T3 (local or regional paper). Move NYC 3 to 2 and London 3 to 2; impact is small (6 reviews).

name: Londonist
justification: Londonist is a London city news and guide site, formerly part of the Gothamist network and run by LDN Creative since 2010. Theatre reviews are an incidental strand of a general city-life publication, with 4 reviews in our data and no aggregator pickup found. T4 fits; keep.

name: Attitude
justification: Attitude is a British gay lifestyle magazine founded in 1994. Its 3 theatre pieces in our data come from 3 different staff writers, theatre is incidental to its coverage, and its scores sit far above established critics on that tiny sample (bias +19.6). No theatre critic found. T4 fits. Keep.

name: The Queer Review
justification: The Queer Review is a queer arts and culture site covering film, TV, theatre, music and books; theatre is one section among several. I could not find an about page or verify the editor or critic credentials of James Kleinmann. Not enough to move, so keep T4.

name: Popbytes
justification: PopBytes is a Los Angeles music blog founded in 2003 by Michael Knudsen; Alex Nagorski is its theater editor and wrote all 5 reviews here, mostly of Los Angeles productions. Theatre is a side topic of a music and celebrity blog, and no critics'-body membership was found. That fits T4 (incidental theatre coverage, no recognition); move 3 to 4.

name: NJArts
justification: NJArts.net is a New Jersey arts news and events site run by a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, free to read and funded by donations; its homepage notes it has announced its closure. Our five reviews are by Jay Lustig, whose background could not be verified with the search budget available. A regional arts site with its own staff bylines fits T3; keep.

name: Toronto Star
justification: The Toronto Star is a major Canadian daily. Most of its reviews here are by Richard Ouzounian, its chief theatre critic from 2000 to 2015 and Variety's Canadian theatre correspondent from 2002 to 2013, called Toronto's most influential critic by Toronto Life. It is a market-setting paper in Toronto but an occasional visitor to New York (5 reviews), so T3 for the NYC market is reasonable. KEEP.

name: The Jewish Voice and Opinion
justification: The Jewish Voice and Opinion is a community publication on Jewish culture and politics whose theatre column, 'Two Sues on the Aisle', is written by two contributors with a challah rating scale. Small community outlet with no recognized critics found; keep T4.

name: Dread Central
justification: Dread Central is an American horror news and review website founded in 2006; its 2 theatre reviews in our data cover horror-themed shows. Theatre coverage is incidental. One reviewer, Caroline Cao, is an Outer Critics Circle member and writes for theatre outlets, but two genre pieces do not make the outlet a theatre publication. Keep T4.

name: Nyc Theatre Addict
justification: NYC Theatre Addict is a personal blog by a retired high school theatre teacher who writes about trips to New York to see shows ('About Me'). It is single-author, with no editor, no outside recognition and no critic credentials found. That matches T4 exactly; propose nyc4 (5 rows, low impact).

name: Third Coast Review
justification: Third Coast Review is a Chicago arts and culture publication published by Third Coast Review LLC, with sections from art to film and a Stages section, many contributing writers, reader support via Patreon, and membership in the Chicago Independent Media Alliance. That is a regional multi-contributor arts outlet, which fits T3. Keep.

name: Vogue
justification: Vogue is Conde Nast's fashion magazine; its rare theater reviews (6 from 2015 to 2025) were written by editors such as Chloe Schama. A major national magazine with only occasional theater coverage and no dedicated critic fits T3. KEEP.

name: Theatre South East
justification: Theatre South East was launched in November 2014 by Sammi O'Neill to promote theatre in London and the South East; it runs reviews, interviews and competitions, sells West End tickets and recruits other bloggers. That is close to the T4 description (small site, promotional purpose), but with only 8 rows, ordinary consensus numbers and some contributor structure, the evidence is not clear enough to move. Keep.

name: Slate
justification: Slate is a US national online magazine of politics and culture, founded in 1996 and owned by The Slate Group (Graham Holdings). It has no dedicated theatre critic listed; its 4 reviews (2018 to 2026) are by its culture writers. Incidental theatre coverage argues for a lower tier, but it is an established professional publication with paid critics and only 4 reviews, so the evidence is not strong enough to move; keep.

name: Gizmodo
justification: Gizmodo is a technology, science and science-fiction website, owned by Keleops Media since June 2024. Its single theater review in our data is by an io9 pop-culture writer covering a genre musical. Theater coverage is incidental, which fits T4; keep.

name: W42st
justification: W42ST describes itself as a hyperlocal media brand celebrating Hell's Kitchen, operated by KOB Publishing LLC. Its one review here is from Michael Musto's monthly column, and Musto is a long-established former Village Voice columnist. One review from a hyperlocal community site does not show sustained theatre criticism, so keep T4.

name: Yale Daily News
justification: The Yale Daily News is a student newspaper at Yale University, founded in 1878, run entirely by students who make all editorial decisions. Our single review is by a student writer. Student criticism with no recognized-critic status fits T4; keep.

name: Another Eye Opens
justification: Another Eye Opens is Don Shewey's personal Substack of 'cultural commentary', mixing reporting, recommendations and archive pieces. Shewey has freelanced for the New York Times, Village Voice, Esquire and Rolling Stone and written three books about theater, so he is an established writer, but the newsletter is a single-author personal outlet with one review in our data. KEEP nyc4; a move is not justified on one review.

name: Jonathan Baz
justification: jonathanbaz.com is a Blogger blog whose footer says all content is owned by Jonathan Baz; nearly every post is his, with an occasional guest review (for example one by Emma Kaabachi), and it is active (posts dated October 2026). There is no about page, bio, editor or critics' body membership on the site, and two searches found no outside coverage or aggregator quotes of Baz or the blog. Its scores run much kinder than established critics (bias +11.1, gap 15.8 over 17). A single-author blog with no recognition is the T4 definition; the London move from 3 to 4 is confirmed (NYC unused, aligned).

name: Boston.com
justification: Boston.com is the Boston Globe group's free news site; its recent review is in a community section by Samantha Genzer, with no role stated, and one older review is by AP's Mark Kennedy. With 5 reviews and an unclear contributor status, there is not enough to move; keep.

name: San Francisco Chronicle
justification: The San Francisco Chronicle is a major Bay Area daily newspaper founded in 1865, and its reviews in our data are touring productions reviewed mainly by its theatre critic Lily Janiak. It is a professional regional paper with a staff critic, which matches the T3 'local or regional papers' definition for this market. Keep. Critics' body membership for Janiak was not verified.

name: Digital Spy
justification: Digital Spy has no reviews in our data, so there is nothing to weigh and it does not affect any score. It is a UK entertainment site whose theatre coverage would be incidental, but this was not verified this pass (search budget ran out). Keep.
